# 44. What the sms move leaves in femcore

Date: 2026-11-04

## Status

Accepted (restructure phase 4, bookmark `restructure-4-sms`). Records the seams between the sms and ems moves, which ran in parallel.

## Context

The solid kernels shared a few things with the electromagnetic ones, and the two moves were done by separate sessions that must merge without either rewriting the other's files.

## Decision

Stays in `femcore`, used by `nyx-sms` as it is:

* `periodic` (Floquet reduction of dofs: `match_vertices`, `nodal_relations`, `Reduction`, `congruence`): shared with `ems3d`; neither move touches it.
* `ems_pml::cell_stretches` (the complex stretch factors of a perfectly matched layer per cell): used by `sms::pml` and `sms::cross_section`. It is public in `femcore` and **must stay public there or move to a shared place** (`props` is the candidate) when `ems_pml` moves into `nyx-ems`; `nyx-sms` must then change one import. `section::mesh_pml_dirs` it relies on stays.
* `section`, `material`, `fields`, `fem`, `optical`, `polarization`, `analysis`, `props`: as ADR 41 says.

Small changes in shared files, each a few lines, listed so the merge can be checked:

* `progress::lap_since(&mut Instant, label)` replaces `sms::lap`, which `fem.rs`, `ems3d.rs` and `linalg/amg_elastic` called for stage timings (six lines in `ems3d.rs`, three in `fem.rs`, seven in `amg_elastic/mod.rs`). If the ems move deletes `ems3d.rs` or edits those lines, take its version and call `progress::lap_since`.
* `validate::non_finite_token` is `pub` (the typed problem's finite check scans tensors and layers for the words NaN and inf).
* `solve.rs` answers an error for `Physics::Solid` as it does for the dfs arms; `lib.rs` loses the six `sms*` modules. `femcore::problem` and the old `ProblemSpec` stay for the window until phase 7.
* `h5io`'s round-trip test builds a solid-shaped result by hand (the kernel is no longer in femcore), like its heat one.

## Consequences

* The three crates `nyx-dfs`, `nyx-sms`, `nyx-ems` depend on `femcore` only; the layering test is unchanged by this move.
* Until the ems move lands, `femcore::solve` still runs `ems`.

## Code

`crates/femcore/src/{progress,validate,solve,lib,h5io}.rs`, `crates/nyx-sms/src/pml.rs`.
decisions.title: What the sms move leaves in femcore

decisions.content:
# 45. The electromagnetic kernels move into `nyx-ems`; what they share with the analysis and the solid kernels stays in `femcore`

Date: 2026-11-04

## Status

Accepted (restructure phase 4, bookmark `restructure-4-ems`). Carries out ADR 41 for `ems` (the second physics after `dfs`). Closes ROUGH_SPOTS R10 (the EM study is named, not guessed from the dimension of the mesh). Builds on ADR 25 (the `Physics` trait), ADR 9 (three stages) and ADR 12 (codes).

## Context

`femcore` had four EM modules: `ems` (real full-vector modes of a 2D cross-section), `ems_pml` (the same in complex arithmetic: absorbing layers, loss, a crystal tilted against the guide), `ems_axisym` (bodies of revolution) and `ems3d` (3D cavities and Floquet cells). They read the old `ProblemSpec` and dispatched on the dimension of the mesh. Three things outside them used their internals: `optical` (the field sampler of the polarization analysis builds on the edge-element basis and on the complex material tensors, and its `solve_optical` called the mode solvers), the solid kernels (`sms_pml`, `sms_kz` used the PML stretch of `ems_pml`), and the use cases (`usecases/{soi,bragg}` called `solve::solve`). `femcore` cannot depend on `nyx-ems` (the crate depends on `femcore`), and `analysis`, `polarization` and `optical` stay in `femcore` until phase 5 because the old `SolveResult` carries an `Analysis`.

## Decision

1. **Crate layout.** `nyx-ems` holds `problem` (typed `Problem`, `Study`, `decode`), `modes` (real modes), `modes_complex`, `axisym`, `cavity` (the `ems3d` kernel), `optical` (modes as the field-evaluable set, `solve_optical[_wafer]`) and, in `lib.rs`, the `Ems` physics, `run` and `run_analysed`. Kernels were copied and edited only for types (ADR 41, item 2): same formulas, same order of operations, which is why the goldens keep their numbers.
2. **The study names the kernel.** `modes` (2D), `axisymmetric_modes` (2D, the (r, z) half plane) and `cavity` (3D). `Physics::validate` and the kernels refuse a study on a mesh of the other dimension by name ("the study 'cavity' needs a 3D mesh"). The dispatch on the mesh dimension survives only in the bridge (ADR 47), because the old problem has no kind for it.
3. **What stays in `femcore`, and why.** `edge` (Whitney and degree-2 Nedelec basis on a triangle, per-cell numbering and signs), `pml` (`stretch`, `cell_stretches`) and, in `optical`, the vacuum constants including `C0`, `EpsC`/`MuC` and `cell_materials[_signed]`. They are what the field sampler and the solid kernels share with the EM kernels, so they sit below both. `periodic` (Floquet pairs), `section`, `material`, `fields`, `fem`, `analysis`, `polarization` also stay. `section::axes_of_3d_periodic` is the same function as `axes_of_3d_problem` taking the Floquet pairs alone. `Analysis::summary` is what `attach` adds to scalars and log, for results that are not the old `SolveResult`.
4. **Polarization stays in the result for now.** The 2D and cavity studies compute the polarization with `femcore::analysis` (as before the move) and put the scalars `polarization N` and the table into the new result; `run_analysed` returns the `Analysis` next to it for the window. That keeps the goldens, which record those scalars, identical. Phase 5 moves the computation into `nyx-analysis`, removes the scalars from the result, and rewrites the goldens deliberately (ADR 10).
5. **Descriptors (contract `physics_ems` 1.1).** The fields are scalar arrays under the flat names of the window and of the goldens (`|E|`, `|Exz|`, `|Ey|`, `Ex`, `Ey`, `Ez`; `Re Ex`, ... for complex modes and cavities), because the old results were not a vector field with components and the goldens compare these names. The axisymmetric study takes `f_search` (Hz), a signed `azimuthal_order` and `n_modes`; `n_target` is gone (the kernel searches by frequency). The shape of a result is pinned by `physics_ems_result` 1.0.
6. **Goldens and tests.** Five goldens (`emw_pec_straight`, `emw_pec_tilted`, `emw_pml_x`, `emw_soi_wire`, `emw_soi_hybrid`) moved unchanged to `crates/nyx-ems/tests/golden/`; the first three keep their tolerances (1e-7). The two silicon-wire files never reproduced on this machine (R22); gate G2 (option B) sets their tolerances to 5e-5 relative on n_eff and 1e-3 of the field maximum, with the class of the polarization compared as text. The ems tests of `emw2d`, `emw3d`, `pml`, `aniso_optics`, `bragg_stack`, `photonics`, `physics_meshing`, the SOI tests of `meshing` and the ems test of `anisotropic`, `frame_roundtrip`, `stages`, `adapt3d`, `wafer_names` and `ring_frame` moved with the kernels, with the same numbers and tolerances. `femcore::solve` answers an error for `Physics::Emw`.

## Consequences

* Positive: `ems` is a crate with its own problem type; the window keeps working through the bridge; the stage API is contract-tested in the crate; every moved golden passes with unchanged numbers (the two SOI files at G2 tolerances).
* Negative: `nyx-ems` depends on `femcore::analysis` until phase 5; four small shared modules sit in `femcore` only because of the crate direction; the envelope carries scalar permittivity only (crystal tensors reach the kernel through the typed problem until the material files, phase 6).
* The imports `crate::ems_pml::cell_stretches` in `sms_pml.rs` and `sms_kz.rs` are now `crate::pml::cell_stretches`; the sms thread's copies of those files need the same one-line change at the merge.
* Open: `Physics::sizing` still returns the placeholder (the wavelength per region is read by `physics_size::spec_sizing` from the old spec); the adapters go when the window is rewired (phase 7).

## Code

`crates/nyx-ems/src/*`, `crates/femcore/src/{edge,pml,optical}.rs`, `crates/nyx-engine/src/legacy/ems.rs`.

## Contract

`physics_ems.v1.json` 1.1, `physics_ems_result.v1.json` 1.0, the stage-API test in `crates/nyx-ems/tests/contracts.rs`.
decisions.title: The electromagnetic kernels move into `nyx-ems`; what they share with the analysis and the solid kernels stays in `femcore`

decisions.content:
# 46. The axisymmetric EM kernel is checked against closed forms and gets a study (gate G1)

Date: 2026-11-04

## Status

Accepted (restructure phase 4, bookmark `restructure-4-ems`). Answers the G1 action for the `ems_axisym` half (paul: keep the axisymmetric kernels, but check their implementation before they move). The solid half (`sms_axisym`) is the sms thread's.

## Context

`ems_axisym` solves the modes of a body of revolution at azimuthal order `m` (`exp(-j m theta)`, theta along wafer +y) on the (r, z) half plane: `E_r, E_z` in the degree-2 Nedelec space of the waveguide solver and `E_theta` in P2, a Hermitian pencil `curl-curl x = (omega/c)^2 eps x`. Before this phase it had no study: nothing in `ProblemSpec` could ask for it, and it was reached only by tests. Paul was not sure of the implementation.

## What was verified

All numbers are in `crates/nyx-ems/tests/axisym.rs` (run with `--nocapture` for the printed errors), second-order elements:

* **Coaxial cavity, PEC, `a < r < b`, `0 < z < h`, m = 0**: the TEM modes have `f = p c / (2h)` for any `a`, `b`. Relative errors 1.4e-6 (p = 1) and 8e-6 (p = 2). The same cavity at m = 1 has nothing at the TEM frequency.
* **PEC cylinder cavity, TM modes at m = 1, 2, 3**: `f = c x_{m,1} / (2 pi R)` with `x_{m,1}` the first zero of the Bessel function `J_m`. This is the check the coaxial case cannot make: it exercises the `m / r` terms of the curl and the `E_theta` unknown. A thin rod of radius `a` on the axis keeps the mesh off the axis: relative errors 1.1e-5 (m = 2) and 2.7e-5 (m = 3); at m = 1 the error is 1.3e-3 with a 2 mm rod and 3.5e-4 with a 1 mm rod, so the rest at m = 1 is the rod (about `(a/R)^2` times a factor), not the discretisation.
* **Direction**: for a silicon wire in silica on a 20 mm ring, `m > 0` and `m < 0` give the same frequency and the power along theta (wafer y) is positive for `m > 0` and negative for `m < 0`, equal in size to 1e-3.

## What was not verified

* A dielectric whispering-gallery mode against an analytic or independent reference (only the symmetry in `m` and the sign of the power are checked); the Bessel-zero test is the closest independent check of the azimuthal terms.
* Absorbing layers in the axisymmetric kernel (`AxiMaterial::with_pml`, stretch of `r` with `r~`/`r` for the azimuthal component) are exercised by the code path of the `pml` BC but not compared with a closed form or with a larger domain. Open boundaries are not modelled otherwise: the walls are perfect conductors, adequate for well-confined modes in a large enough domain.
* Order 1 elements, large `m` (the mesh must resolve `m / r`), meshes that touch the axis (not supported; the mesh must stay off `r = 0`).

## Decision

1. The kernel moves unchanged (same formulas) into `nyx_ems::axisym`.
2. It gets a study, `axisymmetric_modes` (parameters `f_search`, signed `azimuthal_order`, `n_modes`), a fields stage (`axisym_fields_cells`: `|E|` and `Re Ex` (r), `Re Ey` (theta), `Re Ez` (z) with the phase rotated so the largest component is real, plus complex per-cell components), and a solve (`solve_axisymmetric`): permittivity and permeability per domain from `eps_r` and `mu_r`, absorbing layers from the `pml` condition (`x` is the r direction, `z` the z direction). `AxiMaterial::from_materials` builds the material data. Results: one solution per mode with its frequency (`value`), scalars `f N (Hz)` and `Q N` when the layers make it complex.
3. The G1 note in the status file is satisfied by the list above; the gaps are open items for whoever uses the kernel for a real resonator.

## Consequences

* The kernel is reachable from the envelope and from the engine; it has no goldens (there is nothing frozen from the old code to compare with) and its tests are closed forms.
* The window cannot ask for it (the old problem has no axisymmetric EM study); it appears with the engine commands in phase 7.

## Code

`crates/nyx-ems/src/axisym.rs`, `crates/nyx-ems/tests/axisym.rs`.

## Contract

`physics_ems.v1.json` 1.1 (the `axisymmetric_modes` study), `physics_ems_result.v1.json`.
decisions.title: The axisymmetric EM kernel is checked against closed forms and gets a study (gate G1)

# 47. `ems` in the legacy bridge, and the use cases take their solver as an argument

Date: 2026-11-04

## Status

Accepted (restructure phase 4, bookmark `restructure-4-ems`). Applies ADR 41, item 6, to `ems`; amends ADR 22 (use cases live in `femcore`) for how they solve.

## Context

The window and the MCP session still build the old `ProblemSpec` for EM waves and read the old `SolveResult`, including its `analysis` (the Stokes parameters and the Poincare sphere). The old problem has no EM study kind: a 2D mesh meant waveguide modes, a 3D mesh meant a cavity. The use cases `usecases::soi` and `usecases::bragg` solved by calling `femcore::solve::solve`, which cannot reach `nyx-ems`; they are used by the window (the example projects), the MCP session (`slab_neff`, wire parameters), tests and examples.

## Decision

1. **`nyx_engine::legacy::ems`** converts the old problem to `nyx_ems::Problem` (`problem_from_old`): a 2D mesh with a `Modes` study is `Study::Modes`, a 3D mesh with an `Eigenfrequency` study is `Study::Cavity`; any other combination answers the text the old dispatch gave ("mode analysis needs a Modes study", "EM waves on a 3D mesh use the Eigenfrequency study"). Materials (scalars, crystals, PML) and Floquet pairs are copied. It runs `nyx_ems::run_analysed`, converts the result with `result_back` and puts the `Analysis` into `SolveResult::analysis`. `legacy::solve_with` routes `Physics::Emw` there; `femcore::solve` answers an error.
2. **Use cases get a solver.** `usecases::Solver` is a function from a mesh and an old spec to an old result. `SoiWire::solve`, `BraggGrating::{solve, band_edges, band_edges_of, bragg_frequency_estimate, matched_period}`, `fundamental_neff` and `group_index` take one. The window, the tests and the examples pass `nyx_engine::legacy::solve`. The geometry, mesh and spec parts of the use cases are unchanged and still in `femcore`, so the `nyx-ems` golden tests can use `SoiWire` without the bridge. The use cases and the bridge are deleted together in phase 7 (the plan retires `usecases/`).
3. **Where the mixed tests went.** `usecases.rs` (it needs the old result with its analysis) is `crates/nyx-engine/tests/usecases.rs`; the studies and benchmarks `soi_modes`, `bragg_gratings`, `cavity_bench` and `complex_bench` are `crates/nyx-engine/examples/` (`tools/baseline.sh` runs `cavity_bench` from there). Every other ems test is in `crates/nyx-ems/tests/` and runs the typed problem directly.

## Consequences

* The window behaves as before: same results, same analysis tab, same log text.
* `femcore` has no EM solver left; `femcore::solve` is down to `sms`.
* Two result shapes still exist until phase 7, as for `dfs`.

## Code

`crates/nyx-engine/src/legacy/ems.rs`, `crates/femcore/src/usecases/*`, `crates/nyx-engine/tests/usecases.rs`, `crates/nyx-engine/examples/*`.

## Contract

`kernel_stages` 1.3 (the ems stages are checked in `crates/nyx-ems/tests/contracts.rs`).

# 5. Meshes stay native: one cell type per cell, simplex split only as a fallback

Date: 2026-11-02

## Status

**Implemented end to end by ADR 32 and 52 (see ADR 65).** Accepted as a constraint on the mesher side (paul, 2026-11-02, quoted in `docs/ports/meshers/FEATURE_DEPENDENCIES.md`). The solver side that consumes native cells is being written elsewhere and does not exist in this repository.

## Context

The structured PML layers are quadrilaterals (2D) and prisms and hexahedra (3D). Cutting them into simplices doubles the cell count (2D) or multiplies it by 3 to 6 (3D) and gives different finite-element spaces than the native cells. The solvers are being upgraded, so nothing should assume simplex-only or low order.

## Decision

* Meshes are native `CellMesh` values with a **type per cell** (Tri, Quad, Tet, Prism, Hex). `pml3::PmlBox::cells` and `meshing_pml::structured_pml_native` hold the uncut cells in nyx's tensor-product node order (quad `0,1,3,2` around the cell).
* The simplex split (`SimplexMesh::from_cells_split`) is a **fallback** that lets today's simplex-only solvers run; it is conforming because it depends only on global vertex ids.
* The mesher keeps its own dimension-generic types (`meshers::cellmesh::CellMesh<D>`, `meshers::mesh::SimplexMesh<D>`) as working types; `meshers::interop` translates at the border, including node order, and facets become the elements of one dimension lower with 0-based numbers.
* The mesher assumes no maximum element order and the Nedelec families; it states its node-order conventions in `meshers/cellmesh.rs` (Tri/Quad counter-clockwise, Tet right-handed, Hex bottom quad then top, Prism base then top with the handedness opposite to the VTK wedge).

## Consequences

* Two `CellMesh` types coexist (R01) and the label bases differ between them (R09). One of them has to go when the solver interface is fixed; the open questions are on the solver side (cell types and node orders it wants, whether boundary quads and triangles are both expected).
* The 3D PML box (`pml3`) and `meshers::adapt::pml` generate the same structure twice (R04).
* Nothing consumes native cells today; they are checked only by counts, orientation and split equivalence.

## Code

`crates/femcore/src/cellmesh.rs`, `meshers/cellmesh.rs`, `meshers/interop.rs`, `meshers/adapt/pml.rs`, `pml3.rs`, `meshing_pml.rs`. History: `b9a135e`, `154b64e`, `79936d6`.

## Contract

`contracts/mesh`: pins the node-order permutations of `interop` and the label bases.
decisions.title: Meshes stay native: one cell type per cell, simplex split only as a fallback

# 50. Wavelength sizing in 3D: one element size per region, asked from the neutral `Sizing`

Date: 2026-11-05

## Status

Accepted (bookmark `restructure-4m-mesh3d-features`). Carries ADR 32 step 6 (the neutral `femcore::meshing::Sizing`) into 3D; lifts the "wavelength sizing is not extended to 3D" item of ADR 40. Paul: adaptive meshing, wavelength sizing and structured PML are essential in 3D.

## Context

A physics reports the shortest wavelength it wants resolved in every region (`Sizing { order, headroom, wavelengths: name -> metres }`); the mesher turns it into element sizes with its points-per-wavelength calibration (`physics_size::cell_sizes_for`: 12 per wavelength at order 1, 6 at order 2, relaxed by `pml_relax` in absorbing pieces). In 2D `mesh_for_problem` did this for a `ProblemSpec`, with a global size (simple mesher) or a metric (adaptive mesher). In 3D it answered an error, because it called the 2D mesher; and `physics_size::metrics` is 2D only.

## Decision

* **`meshing::mesh_for_sizing(list, plan, sizing, sz)`** takes the neutral `Sizing` and works in either dimension. Region names are resolved with the label map of the model (a name the model does not have is an error, never silence); absorbing pieces are known from the model (`Evaluated::pml_regions`). In 2D it is `mesh_for_problem` without a `ProblemSpec` (both now share `mesh_waves_2d`, which changes no number). `mesh_for_problem` answers a clear error for a 3D model and points to `mesh_for_sizing`.
* **A size per region, not one global size.** In 3D the lattice mesher already refines a region that asks for a finer element than the global one (Rivara bisection, ADR 40). The wave size of a region is therefore handed to `GeomDomain3` as one more request on the region (`Sizes3::region_h`, finer only: the plan's `h` stays the ceiling, as in 2D), next to the `Size` rules and the layers of an absorbing piece. A cavity with a glass ball (wavelength 0.6, `h` 0.1) in air (wavelength 2.4, `h` 0.4) gets 0.1 in the ball and 0.4 in the air; 2D could only use the smallest size everywhere with the simple mesher.
* **The lattice is made at the coarsest size any meshed region needs** (never above the plan's `h`), and the finer regions are refined from it. A study whose waves are short everywhere is meshed at the right size at once instead of at a coarse size and bisected afterwards.
* **Adaptive mesher.** The start mesh is made from the model's own sizes (as in 2D); the metric is the intersection of the geometry metric (`adapt3d::vertex_sizes3`) and the wave size, both times `Adaptive::scale`, so `scale` stays one knob (ADR 51).
* Not done: curvature or corner sizing of the waves (calibration stays on the mesher side, `MISSING_FEATURES.md` E6); anisotropic sizes (the metric is isotropic, as in 2D).

## Consequences

* The engine (`FemcoreMesher::mesh`) can drop its "physics sizing is unsupported" answer for 3D models once it calls `mesh_for_sizing` or `mesh_request` (ADR 54); not done here (outside `meshing` and `adapt`).
* Measured (`tests/mesh3d_features.rs`): the ball above has 20 times the cells of the unsized mesh, the mean longest edge in the ball is below 0.13 for a wanted 0.1 (bisection ratio 1.3), the air stays at 0.2 or more; volumes are as exact as before.

## Code

`crates/femcore/src/meshing/{mod,geomdrive3}.rs` (`mesh_for_sizing`, `wave_sizes_by_region`, `Sizes3`, `GeomDomain3::new_with`).

## Contract

`mesh_request_and_report_match_their_exemplars_and_schemas` (the request carries the `Sizing`), behaviour in `crates/femcore/tests/mesh3d_features.rs` (`wavelength_sizing_*`, `absorbing_pieces_are_relaxed_by_pml_relax`).
decisions.title: Wavelength sizing in 3D: one element size per region, asked from the neutral `Sizing`

# 51. Adaptive meshing of 3D geom models: `adapt3` with the exact faces as the oracle

Date: 2026-11-05

## Status

Accepted (bookmark `restructure-4m-mesh3d-features`). Lifts "the adaptive mesher and error estimators are not extended to 3D" of ADR 40. Uses ADR 11 (determinism), ADR 18 (no curved elements), ADR 40 (lattice mesher), ADR 50 (wave sizes).

## Context

`Mesher::Adaptive` meant the 2D metric adaptation. In 3D the pieces existed apart: the start mesh (ADR 40), `adapt::drive3::adapt3` (split, collapse, flip, edge removal, smoothing on tetrahedra, with surfaces, creases and corners classified from the start mesh itself) and an oracle trait `Geometry3` that only knew triangles of the start mesh or a hand-given sphere projector. Run on a curved model, `adapt3` shrank the body (every new surface vertex lies on a chord) and it never carried the interface facets of ADR 40 through.

## Decision

`Mesher::Adaptive` on a 3D model is: lattice start mesh, a vertex metric, `adapt3_with` (`meshing::adapt3d`).

* **The oracle** (`GeomOracle3`, `FaceTable`). A surface vertex slides over its patch and a new one lands on the nearest *exact* geom face among the faces of the patch's signature (`Complex::facet_project`: plane, sphere, torus, cylinder wall); a boundary patch takes the faces of its boundary number, an interface patch the faces between exactly its two domains. Creases and corners keep the polylines of the start mesh: straight creases (boxes, layer stacks, ribs) are exact, curved ones as good as the start mesh, like the lattice mesher (ADR 40).
* **Creases are by label, not by angle.** `TopoOptions3::crease_angle_deg` is 120 for geom models: faces with different signatures always meet in a crease, but a coarse facetted sphere (dihedral angles above 40 degrees) is not a crease that pins its vertices to the chords. A same-label fold stays safe because the oracle projects onto the nearest exact face of that label.
* **Interface facets.** `Work3::to_mesh` returns outer boundary facets only and `Work3::from_mesh` rejects interior facets. The interface facets of the lattice mesh are removed before and written back after, labelled by the nearest geom face between the two domains (`FaceTable::interface_label`, the rule of `GeomDomain3::boundary_label`), oriented out of the lower-numbered domain.
* **Sizes** (`vertex_sizes3`, `a_priori_metrics3`, `geometry_floor3`): region sizes (global, `Size` rules, layers of absorbing pieces), the chord limit `2 sqrt(2 r max_dev)` on spheres, and the wave sizes of ADR 50. `geometry_floor3` is the part the geometry insists on, the floor of an estimator metric (ADR 53). Size rules on edges are not meaningful for the lattice and stay ignored.
* **Options for geom models** (`Adaptive` maps to `AdaptOptions3`): at most 12 iterations, stop at 2 % of the tetrahedra changed per iteration (a curved surface never lets splits and collapses cancel, so the defaults of 30 and 0.5 % are spent on churn), and `sweep_frac` 0.3 % (see below).
* **Fixes in `adapt3` found on the way** (all in `adapt::{ops3,topo3,drive3}`; the default behaviour of the 3D loops is unchanged except where it was wrong):
  * `edge_removal_pass` could turn a triangle of the ring inside out (the ends of the edge still lay on its two sides), which overlaps the new tetrahedra; the triangles must now all face the way the ring does. It could also create a diagonal that exists elsewhere in the mesh, and a face with four tetrahedra. Edges and faces made earlier in the same pass are tracked (the snapshot does not know them), also in `flip_pass` for the 3-2 and 2-3 flips.
  * `Work3::check` (run after every pass with `FEMMESH_CHECK=1`) now also finds *overlap*: the two tetrahedra of an interior face must lie on opposite sides of it. Positive volumes and at most two tetrahedra per face do not exclude a folded mesh (the symptom was a total volume of 65.95 for a box of 64).
  * Dead tetrahedra were never removed from the working arrays, so every sweep walked an array several times the size of the mesh (`Work3::compact_tets` at the start of every loop of a sweep). `AdaptOptions3::sweep_frac` (default 0: the old rule, repeat until a sweep changes nothing) lets a sweep loop stop when it changes at most that fraction of the tetrahedra; every sweep rebuilds the incidence of the whole mesh.
* Labels pass through unchanged: domains, boundary facets and (rewritten) interface facets keep the numbers of the model's `LabelMap` (contract `mesh_geom3d_adaptive_and_structured_meshes_keep_the_label_map`).

## Consequences

* A sphere of radius 0.9 in a box refined from `h` 0.6 to 0.3: every vertex of the sphere is on the sphere to 1e-6 (the run without the oracle shrinks the ball to 64 % of its volume), the box faces are exact to 1e-14, the total volume is 64 to 1e-14, the mesh is identical for 1, 3 and 8 threads.
* A strongly graded case (wave size 0.15 in a ball inside a box with the start mesh at 0.8, 17 000 tetrahedra) takes about 30 s on this machine (183 s before the fixes and the sweep rule); the passes are still serial (`MISSING_FEATURES.md` T4) and rebuild the incidence per sweep, which is the next thing to make cheaper. The worst quality at the end is about 1e-3 on the sphere (surface flips on curved patches, T1, are not done).
* Not done: curved creases from the exact edges (the polylines of the start mesh), surface flips on curved patches, threaded passes, mixed sweep axes (geom).

## Code

`crates/femcore/src/meshing/adapt3d.rs`, dispatch in `meshing/mod.rs` (`mesh_3d_plan`); fixes in `crates/femcore/src/adapt/{ops3,topo3,drive3}.rs`; the loop that uses it with an estimator in ADR 53.

## Contract

`mesh_geom3d_adaptive_and_structured_meshes_keep_the_label_map` (`tests/contracts.rs`); behaviour in `tests/mesh3d_features.rs` (`the_adaptive_mesher_*`, `adaptation_is_deterministic_*`, `meshes_are_identical_for_any_thread_count`).
decisions.title: Adaptive meshing of 3D geom models: `adapt3` with the exact faces as the oracle

# 52. Structured absorbing layers in 3D for geom models

Date: 2026-11-05

## Status

Accepted (bookmark `restructure-4m-mesh3d-features`). Lifts "the structured PML is 2D" of ADR 40. Uses ADR 32 step 5 (one PML generator, `pml_box::build_pml`, which keeps the physical vertex and cell numbers), ADR 50, ADR 51.

## Context

`PmlMode::Structured` rebuilt the absorbing layers of a 2D model as quadrilaterals around the physical window (`pml_geom::structured_pml`). In 3D `pml3::add_pml_3d` existed for a box-shaped tetrahedral mesh, with no link to a geom model: no domain numbers of the pieces, no boundary labels of the outer wall, no mesher that makes the physical window box-shaped.

## Decision

`PmlMode::Structured` on a 3D model (`meshing::pml_geom3`):

1. **The physical window is meshed alone.** The absorbing pieces of the model are left out of the lattice (`Sizes3::skip`; `GeomDomain3` treats a face between a meshed and a skipped region like a face to the void). The lattice mesher aligns its lattice with the box of the regions it meshes (ADR 40), so the window planes, edges and corners are lattice planes and the physical boundary lies on the window box exactly, which `build_pml` demands. A mesh made the ordinary way (pieces inline) works too: `structured_pml` drops the cells of the pieces; the window planes are surfaces of the model, cut exactly even off the lattice, so the boundary is box-shaped (test `layers_can_replace_the_inline_pieces_of_a_mesh_made_the_ordinary_way`).
2. Optionally the physical mesh is adapted (ADR 51) before the layers are built (the flow of the mesher chart, item P3: adapt the physical mesh, regenerate the layers). Box faces, edges and corners survive adaptation exactly.
3. **`build_pml`** sweeps prisms on the faces, hexahedra on the edges and corners, with the number of layers and the thickness of the `Pml` feature (face pieces; a piece that ends inside the layer, or two pieces of one side that disagree, is an error with a message).
4. **Labels are geom's.** Layer cells take the domain number of the absorbing piece they fill (`air.pml_xmax`, edge and corner pieces included; found by stretch direction and parent material); the outer wall takes the number of the geom face it lies on (nearest outer face of the piece); facets of the physical window that face a layer are interior now and are gone.
5. **Two meshes come out.** `structured_pml_3d_native` returns the uncut `CellMesh<3>` (tetrahedra, prisms, hexahedra; triangular and quadrilateral boundary facets; `CellMesh::check` passes: boundary facets only). `structured_pml_3d` cuts it for the simplex solvers (`SimplexMesh::from_cells_split`), orients every tetrahedron to positive volume (the lattice mesher does; the cut does not), and writes the faces between cells of different domains as facets with the number of the geom face between those two domains, as the inline mesh has them (ADR 40).
* **Physical numbering is kept**: vertices and cells of the physical mesh come first, in the same ids, order, connectivity and labels, in the native and in the cut mesh (contract test, 3D counterpart of the `build_pml` test).
* Restriction: the physical window must be box-shaped (all its boundary on the box faces); a physical region that is not (its boundary meets the box faces and something else) is refused by `build_pml` with its message. A model whose absorbing pieces belong to no meshed region (a sphere cavity in a hole host, whose host is the only region with pieces) has no layers to build.

## Consequences

* Volumes of every domain agree with the inline mesh to 1e-9 of the box; labels equal; conformity (boundary facets = faces of the void plus faces between domains) holds.
* The physics side needs nothing new: `MeshedGeom::pml_materials` already keys the stretch by domain number in 3D.
* The adaptation of a mesh *with* layers is not supported (the layers are rebuilt from the physical mesh each time, as in 2D).

## Code

`crates/femcore/src/meshing/{pml_geom3,pml_geom,geomdrive3,mod}.rs`.

## Contract

`mesh_geom3d_structured_pml_keeps_the_physical_vertex_and_cell_numbers`, `mesh_geom3d_adaptive_and_structured_meshes_keep_the_label_map` (`tests/contracts.rs`); `tests/mesh3d_features.rs` (`structured_layers_*`).
decisions.title: Structured absorbing layers in 3D for geom models

# 53. A Maxwell residual estimator for edge elements, and an adaptation loop that takes any estimator

Date: 2026-11-05

## Status

Accepted (bookmark `restructure-4m-mesh3d-features`). Item E1 of `docs/ports/meshers/FEATURE_DEPENDENCIES.md`, section 2 of `MISSING_FEATURES.md` ("Lowest-order edge elements"). Uses ADR 51 for the adaptation of geom models.

## Context

The solve-estimate-adapt loop of `adapt::estimate3` reads plotted nodal fields and recovers a Hessian. For edge (Nedelec) elements it works at order 2 (2.6e-6 on 494 tetrahedra against 1.8e-4 on 696 uniform ones for a cavity mode) and does not at order 1 (1.2e-2 on 1490 against 5.3e-3 on 696): the field is piecewise linear and only tangentially continuous, so its Hessian is noise. The loop also fixed both the estimator (fields by name) and the adaptation (`adapt3` with the facets of the start mesh), so a geom model could not use the exact faces (ADR 51).

## Decision

* **`adapt::maxwell`: the residual estimator of Beck, Hiptmair, Hoppe and Wohlmuth** for `curl (1/mu) curl E - k0^2 eps E = 0`. Per tetrahedron: `h_T^2 ||curl (1/mu) curl E - k0^2 eps E||^2 + h_T^2 ||div (eps E)||^2` plus half the face terms `h_F ||n x [(1/mu) curl E]||^2 + h_F ||[eps E . n]||^2` of its faces (the tangential trace of `E` is continuous). A boundary face is a perfect conductor (nothing) unless its label is declared natural (a magnetic wall or symmetry plane: `h_F ||n x (1/mu) curl E||^2`). `maxwell_indicators` returns `eta_T^2` and the four parts summed.
* **The field comes through one trait**, `CurlField::sample(cell, lam) -> (E, curl E)` at a barycentric point, complex, polynomial of degree at most 2 in the cell (orders 1 and 2) and continued a little outside the cell, because first derivatives are central differences along the barycentric directions (exact for quadratics). The estimator does not know how degrees of freedom are numbered; the physics crates implement the trait for theirs (the test adapter in `nyx-ems` uses `cavity::basis3` and `Ned3`). Nothing in a physics crate is touched by this ADR (`sms` and `ems` are being moved in parallel).
* **`indicator_metrics`: equidistribution.** A cell of size `s` (the edge of the regular tetrahedron of its volume) with indicator `eta` asks for `s (tau / eta)^(1/(order + 3/2))`, kept within a factor 4 of `s` and between `h_min_fraction * h_max` and `h_max`; `tau` is found by bisection so that the predicted cell count `sum (s / s_new)^3` equals the target. A vertex takes the smallest size of its cells; the result is an isotropic metric, intersected with an optional floor (`adapt3d::geometry_floor3` for geom models).
* **`estimate3::adapt_loop3`**: the loop of `solve_adaptively3` with the two choices passed in: what the solution asks of the mesh (`metrics`) and how a mesh is adapted to it (`adapt`). `solve_adaptively3` is now a call of it with the Hessian estimator and the plain `adapt3`; its behaviour is unchanged (cell counts of the existing tests are identical). For a geom model `adapt` is `adapt3d::adapt_to_metrics3`.
* Limits: real isotropic coefficients, no source term, absorbing layers are left out (`skip`: their coefficients are complex tensors), eigenmodes and homogeneous problems. Goal-oriented (dual-weighted) adaptivity is E2 and not done.

## Consequences

Measured on the PEC box cavity 40 x 30 x 20 mm, lowest mode (`crates/nyx-ems/tests/maxwell_estimator.rs`, closed form):

| order | uniform blocks | Hessian loop (earlier) | Maxwell loop |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 5.3e-3 on 696 tets, 6.9e-3 on 1470 | 1.2e-2 on 1490 | **5.2e-4 on 333**, 5.6e-5 on 882 |
| 2 | 1.8e-4 on 696, 6.7e-5 on 1470 | 2.6e-6 on 494 | 1.7e-4 on 345, **8.0e-6 on 1402** |

The total indicator falls by 2.19 per halving of `h` at order 1 and 4.9 at order 2 (rates 1 and 2). On the sphere cavity from geom (loop with `adapt_to_metrics3`, exact sphere as the oracle, curvature floor), the error falls from 1.8e-2 to about 5e-3 in two cycles, where the polyhedral sphere (ADR 18) is the limit for both orders.

## Code

`crates/femcore/src/adapt/{maxwell,estimate3}.rs`.

## Contract

`adapt_maxwell_estimator_contract` (`tests/contracts.rs`: the trait, the four parts adding up, natural boundaries, skipped domains, refusals); the closed-form residual of a field with known curl and the equidistribution in the unit tests of `adapt/maxwell.rs`; `crates/nyx-ems/tests/maxwell_estimator.rs` (needs the cavity kernel: rates, loop against uniform blocks at both orders, the chain on a sphere from geom).
decisions.title: A Maxwell residual estimator for edge elements, and an adaptation loop that takes any estimator

# 54. A mesh is asked for and reported in data

Date: 2026-11-05

## Status

Accepted (bookmark `restructure-4m-mesh3d-features`). New contracts `mesh_request`, `mesh_report` and their schemas (ADR 19). Nothing in the engine or the MCP crates is rewired here; this is what they can call.

## Context

Adaptive meshing, wavelength sizing and structured absorbing layers were Rust structs (`MeshPlan`, `Adaptive`, `PhysicsSizing`) that no command could name, and the engine answers "unsupported" for physics sizing. The engine's commands and the MCP tools are generated from JSON Schemas (ADR 37, 38); the mesh needed a request and a report of the same kind, for 2D and 3D.

## Decision

`femcore::meshing::request`:

* **`MeshRequest`** (serde): `h`, optional `max_dev`, `mesher` (`{"kind": "simple"}` or `{"kind": "adaptive", scale, grade, max_cells}`), `structured_pml`, and optional `waves` (`sizing` = the neutral `Sizing` of a physics, `points_per_wavelength`, `pml_relax`, `eigen_headroom`). `plan()` gives the `MeshPlan`.
* **`mesh_request(list, &request)`** meshes either dimension (`mesh_for_sizing` when there are waves, the plain entry point otherwise) and returns the `MeshedGeom` and a **`MeshReport`**: dimension, vertices, cells, facets, per domain the number of cells and the wave size it asked for, a summary of the adaptation (iterations, converged, capped, worst quality, cells at the start and at the end), and the layers per side of structured layers.
* **JSON Schemas** (draft 2020-12) `request_schema()` and `report_schema()`, checked in as `mesh_request.schema.v1.json` and `mesh_report.schema.v1.json`; exemplars `mesh_request.v1.json` (compared as a value) and `mesh_report.v1.json` (compared by structure: the counts belong to the mesher, not to the contract). `additionalProperties` is false: a typo in a request is an error.

## Consequences

The engine can add a `mesh` argument that is this schema and report this struct without knowing a mesher; the 3D features are reachable through it. The window keeps its own `MeshPlan` use.

## Code

`crates/femcore/src/meshing/request.rs`.

## Contract

`mesh_request_and_report_match_their_exemplars_and_schemas` (`tests/contracts.rs`; a small validator of the schema subset used is part of the test file, no schema crate is needed).
decisions.title: A mesh is asked for and reported in data

# 55. The lattice mesher welds rounding-distance vertices and does not depend on the thread count

Date: 2026-11-05

## Status

Accepted (bookmark `restructure-4m-mesh3d-features`). Amends ADR 40, which listed "a test that the mesh is identical for any `NYX_THREADS` (ADR 11)" as still to add. Found while meshing layer stacks and absorbing windows (ADR 52).

## Context

1. **Slivers.** A surface of the model that lies on a lattice plane (a layer interface at `z = 0`, the faces of an absorbing window) makes the lattice vertices on it count as warped onto the surface, and the lattice edges next to them are also cut, so a cut point can be a few ulp from a warped vertex. The tetrahedra between the two have volume 1e-16 to 1e-30. A box of air over glass at `h` 0.5 had 140 of 3300; their boundary triangles are zero-area, which turned the prisms of the structured layers inside out (`build_pml`: "inverted, scaled Jacobian 0"). The same cells would reach any solver.
2. **Thread count.** Two things in `mesh_3d` depended on how the lattice was divided into blocks, that is on the thread count: the cells were appended block by block as (whole tetrahedra, cut tetrahedra), so the order of the cells changed with the number of blocks, and equal cut ids made by two blocks with different last bits were deduplicated by an unstable sort of the id alone.

## Decision

* After the cells are made and before the facets are derived, every cell edge shorter than `1e-8` of the smallest lattice spacing welds its ends (union-find, representative = lowest id, flags merged); cells with a repeated vertex are dropped. Nothing of ordinary size is touched. With it the same box has a smallest cell volume of 5e-3 (1e-16 before), the structured layers build, and the sliver count of the benchmark models is zero.
* All whole tetrahedra come first, then all cut ones, each in lattice order, independent of the blocks; cut points of equal id are sorted by id and then by position before the deduplication.
* Test: `meshes_are_identical_for_any_thread_count` runs the probe `probe_mesh_hashes` in child processes with `NYX_THREADS` 1, 3 and 8 and compares the hash of points, cells, facets and labels for the simple, adaptive, structured and adaptive-structured plans of a ball in a box with an absorbing window. It failed (the cell order differed from index 19112 on) before the second fix.

## Consequences

Meshes of models without plane-aligned surfaces (the sphere cavity of the benchmark, the torus) are unchanged cell for cell; meshes with them lose their slivers and have a different but equivalent cell numbering. Nothing in the goldens uses a 3D geom mesh.

## Code

`crates/femcore/src/meshing/mesher3d.rs` (steps 4, 5 and 5b).

## Contract

`tests/mesh3d_features.rs` (`meshes_are_identical_for_any_thread_count`, the volume checks of every structured test).
decisions.title: The lattice mesher welds rounding-distance vertices and does not depend on the thread count

# 56. The polarization analysis is a function of a result (`nyx-analysis`)

Date: 2026-11-05

## Status

Accepted (restructure phase 5, bookmark `restructure-5-analysis`). Applies the plan's phase 5 and resolves ROUGH_SPOTS R28; amends ADR 21 (the analysis lived in `femcore`) and ADR 45 and 47 (the mode kernels computed the analysis and the window got it through the result).

## Context

`femcore::{analysis, polarization}` computed the Stokes parameters, Poincare points, mode classes and degenerate groups of optical modes. The `ems` kernels called it at the end of a mode study, wrote one text scalar `polarization N` per mode and the table into the log, and handed the whole `Analysis` out next to the result for the window (`Solved`, `run_analysed`, `SolveResult::analysis` of the old window result). So a result was not just data: a front-end that was not the window, or a stored result, had no way to ask for the analysis, and the analysis could not be changed without touching a physics. The analysis also named its axes after the local frame of the mode solvers (x lateral, y normal, z propagation), so `Ey` meant two things (R28).

## Decision

1. **`nyx-analysis` holds the analysis.** `polarization` (Stokes, Poincare, classes, drawings) and `modes` (`ModeAnalysis`, the table, CSV, groups) moved from `femcore` with their tests; the numbers are unchanged. `polarization(mesh, result)` is the typed entry point; `PolarizationAnalysis` is the same behind the `Analysis` trait (plain JSON). The old struct `Analysis` is `ModeAnalysis` now, so the name is free for the trait. `nyx-analysis` depends on `nyx-physics` and `femcore` (mesh geometry and the quadrature rule); the layering table says so.
2. **A result carries what the analysis needs, not the analysis.** A mode study of `ems` puts the complex electric field of every mode in its cell fields (`Ex`, `Ey`, `Ez` in wafer axes; the 2D kernels already did, the cavity too) and states its **frame** in the scalar `field frame` (`nyx_physics::FieldFrame`): which wafer axes are the lateral, the normal and the propagation direction, the handedness of that triple, and the domains that are absorbing layers and are left out. The text is readable (`lateral x, normal z, propagation y, left-handed, outside domains 2`). A result without a frame is not analysed (`applies_to` is false); the analysis never guesses. The cavity result also has the complex frequency as `Solution::eigenvalue` (Hz), as the field's documentation always said it could.
3. **Sampling.** A cross-section is sampled at the 24 points of `femcore::optical::fine_rule` in every cell outside the absorbing domains, with the field interpolated from the cell nodes (P1 or P2). The mode fields are piecewise quadratic, so this is exact; the reproduced Stokes lines of the five mode goldens agree with the old ones (tests below). A cavity is sampled at the four vertices of every cell, each standing for a quarter of the volume, as before.
4. **The kernels stop computing it.** `Solved`, `run_analysed`, `with_analysis` and the `polarization N` scalars are gone from `nyx-ems`; `nyx_ems::run` returns the result. The table is no longer appended to the log of the new result. The unused public `axisym::mode_samples` and the `optical_set_*` helpers that only fed the analysis were deleted.
5. **The window.** `nyx_engine::legacy::solve_with_analysis` returns the old-shape result and the `ModeAnalysis` of an EM-wave study; `ResultView::analysis` holds it (the old `SolveResult::analysis` is gone). The bridge still appends the table to the old result's log, and sets `Solution::te_fraction` (one number, for the use cases, the run table and nothing else) until phase 7 deletes the old result type. The MCP session reads the analysis from the same call. The engine re-exports the crate as `nyx_engine::analysis` so the window needs no new dependency.
6. **R28.** The samples are `lat`, `nor`, `prop`: what the component is, not an axis number. The documentation maps them to the wafer axes x, z and y; the labels (`quasi-TE (x)`, `quasi-TM (z)`, the `Ey` column for the longitudinal share) were already wafer names and are unchanged, so the Analysis tab reads the same.
7. **Sign convention of the longitudinal field (a fix found on the way).** The real mode solver flips the transverse field so that its largest component is positive but did not flip `E_y` with it, so the relative sign of `E_y` between two modes was arbitrary. The old analysis evaluated the true field and did not see it; an analysis that reads the result does, in the overlap and the resolved pair of a degenerate group. `E_y` is now flipped together with the transverse field, in the plot field and in the cell field. This changes the sign of the `Ey` probe of 6 modes in three goldens (below) and nothing else.

## Consequences

* The five mode goldens lose their `polarization N` scalars and gain `field frame`. The polarization lines they used to hold are kept unchanged in `crates/nyx-ems/tests/golden/polarization.json` and the analysis is checked against them (class as text, rounded numbers to 1.5e-3, 5e-3 for the silicon-wire files at the G2 tolerances). `GOLDEN_CHANGES.md` records both changes.
* Any front-end can run the analysis on a stored result and its mesh; a new physics with complex vector fields can state a frame and get the same analysis.
* `femcore` has no analysis code left; `Solution::te_fraction` and `legacy::solve_with_analysis` go with the old result type in phase 7.
* The analysis table is not in the log of a new-shape result any more; the window's log is unchanged.

## Code

`crates/nyx-analysis/src/{lib,polarization,modes,samples}.rs`, `crates/nyx-physics/src/frame.rs`, `crates/nyx-ems/src/{modes,modes_complex,cavity,optical,lib}.rs`, `crates/nyx-engine/src/legacy/{mod,ems}.rs`, `crates/app/src/{worker,state,app,tabs}.rs`, `crates/nyx-session/src/tools.rs`.

## Contract

`physics_ems_result` 1.1 (scalar `field frame` instead of `polarization N`; the cavity solutions have an eigenvalue). The frame text is documented in `nyx_physics::frame`. No exemplar of its own yet: `analysis_api` is versioned when a second analysis exists.
decisions.title: The polarization analysis is a function of a result (`nyx-analysis`)

# 57. The window and the MCP server are thin front-ends: every tool is an engine command

Date: 2026-11-05

## Status

**Amended by ADR 94** (provisional number, productivity plan S7): the MCP server offers four script tools, `script_run`, `script_wait`, `script_check` and `api`, instead of one tool per engine command, after Paul's answer to Q9 (2026-11-19); the engine commands themselves are unchanged.

Accepted. Implements restructure phase 7. Supersedes the parts of ADR 15 (AI interface: separate workspace, stdio MCP) that describe the `nyx-session` tools, handles and recipes, and the parts of ADR 23 (the app is a shell over one `Project`) that describe `app/state.rs` and `worker.rs`. ADR 41's legacy bridge is deleted.

## Context

After phases 4 to 6 the physics lived in crates behind the `Physics` trait and the engine core (ADR 37, 38) existed with 64 commands, but the two front-ends still used the pre-restructure stack: the window held its own `Project` of the old `femcore::problem::ProblemSpec` and called `nyx_engine::legacy` for solves, and `nyx-mcp` served nine hand-written tools of `nyx-session` (a silicon strip on oxide: `geom_template`, `mesh_make`, `problem_define`, `solve_run`, `result_modes`, `check_run`, `recipe_run`) over `femcore::usecases`. A new physics, a new geometry operation or a new analysis needed edits in three places, and the AI could do less than the window.

## Decision

* **One engine, two front-ends.** `nyx-engine::Engine` holds the project, the mesh, the results and the jobs. The window holds an `Engine` and edits it with commands (`set_problem`, `set_geometry`, `set_mesh`, `add_condition`, `set_material`, `solve_run` through `start_solve`, ...); `nyx-mcp` holds an `Engine` and nothing else. The tool list of the MCP server is `Engine::catalog()` and a tool call is `Engine::call`; the geometry tools are the `add_*` commands generated from the descriptors of the geom operations (ADR 38), all 23, none picked by hand (gate G5).
* **Deleted:** `nyx-session` (its handles, assumptions ledger and recipes), `nyx_engine::legacy`, `femcore::problem` (the old `ProblemSpec`, `SolveResult`, `Study`, `BcKind`), `femcore::usecases` (the SOI wire and the Bragg grating as built-in devices), `femcore::xmlio`, `femcore::h5io`, the XML project format in the window, the built-in material presets and the 18 built-in examples as code. What the person used to get from a use case is a project file (ADR 60) or a sequence of commands (the guide card `nyx-instructions`).
* **MCP behaviour.** `get_guide` is a command (cards in `nyx-engine/cards`). Every result carries `nyx.{session, revision, project_hash}` (the revision counts calls that changed the project). An error is `{error: <code>, message}` with `isError`. The server stores what a host does: the first solve binds the project to a new workflow of the server's workspace folder (origin `ai`), so every solve is a row of the run table and the work shows in the dashboard (`Engine::set_workspace(dir, auto_store)`). The tool list is a new contract version (`mcp_tools.v2.json`; the nine old tools are gone: a major change for hosts, announced in `VERSIONS.md`).
* **The window draws forms from descriptors** (`app/src/forms.rs`): the Study tab, the conditions of the Physics tab and the options of a physics are made from the `ParamDesc`s of the physics, so a new physics needs no change in the window (ADR 25). The Materials tab lists the regions of the model and the files of the library (ADR 58).
* **Layering.** The app depends on `nyx-engine` and `nyx-connect` only; what it draws with and edits (`ViewMesh`, `Display`, the geometry kernel, the store, the physics result types) comes through `nyx_engine::facade`, so the dependency table has no other edge. `nyx-mcp` depends on `nyx-engine` only. The `TEMPORARY` list of the layering test is empty.
* **Not in this step:** `sapphire()` and `silicon()` in `femcore::material` (still used by tests of other crates), the final project layout and its `format` key (phase 8), HDF5 export (an optional engine export, not ported), renaming `experiment.nyx.xml` (phase 8).

## Consequences

* A new geometry operation in `geom` appears in the engine, the MCP server and (through the geometry editor's own forms) the window with the descriptor; a new physics appears in the Physics, Study and Materials tabs and as `add_physics`/`describe_physics` for a host.
* The AI interface has the capabilities of the window (geometry, materials, conditions, mesh, solve, analysis, store). It no longer has a one-call recipe for a silicon strip; the guide shows the sequence. Mesh-convergence checks are done by repeating `solve_run` with a finer `set_mesh`.
* Tests that used the use cases are small generic fixtures (`femcore::testkit::soi`, the example files).

## Code

`crates/nyx-mcp/src/main.rs`, `crates/nyx-engine/src/{commands,guide,analyse,pml}.rs`, `crates/nyx-engine/cards/*.md`, `crates/app/src/{app,state,tabs,forms,examples,shell}.rs`, `crates/nyx-engine/tests/layering.rs`.

## Contract

`mcp_tools.v2` (the tool list), `engine_commands.v1.json` (1.1: the new commands).
decisions.title: The window and the MCP server are thin front-ends: every tool is an engine command

# 58. The engine resolves named materials from the library and the project

Date: 2026-11-05

## Status

Accepted. Implements the wiring of the material files (ADR 29, 30, 34, 35) into the studies that phases 4 and 6 left to phase 7.

## Context

The envelope accepted `MaterialAssign::Named` since phase 4, but every physics answered "material files arrive with phase 6". Phase 6 built the library and the models (`femcore::material`); nothing used them. The window had its own presets and crystal editors, which the new window could not carry.

## Decision

* `MaterialAssign` has a third form, `Oriented { material, euler_deg }`: a named material placed in the wafer frame with Bunge angles. `Named`, `Oriented` and `Props` are told apart by their JSON shape (text, object with `material`, object of numbers).
* `Ctx` carries the material `library` (`femcore::material::Library`) and the free-space `wavelength` of the study. `nyx_physics::decode::materials_by_label` resolves a named material for the properties the physics lists: scalars under the descriptor names (`legacy_scalars`), the crystal data (`Anisotropy`) where the material is anisotropic or rotated, and for a physics that reads `eps_r` the permittivity from the optical model at the wavelength (isotropic: a scalar; birefringent: a tensor in the wafer frame). A material that is lossy at that wavelength is refused by the real-mode solver with a message that points to absorbing layers.
* The **engine** supplies both: `Engine::library()` is the folder library (`materials/` next to the program or in a parent folder, or `NYX_MATERIALS`) with the materials the **project** carries (`Project.materials`: name to TOML text, which may `extends` a library material; added with `add_material`, read at once so a mistake is reported there). The wavelength is `c / f` of the first study parameter of the physics with the unit Hz.
* `Physics::sizing` gets the library (`sizing(&self, spec, library)`) and `ems` and `sms` now state their wavelengths (`optical_wavelength`, `elastic_wavelength` in `femcore::meshing::physics_size`), so `MeshSettings::physics_sizing` works for named materials and anisotropic crystals. The mesher takes a `MeshRequest` (ADR 54): `FemcoreMesher` meshes 2D and 3D models, simple or adaptive, with structured absorbing layers and element sizes from the waves; a 2D model can still be swept along y.
* Commands: `list_materials`, `describe_material`, `add_material`, `remove_material`; `set_material` takes the three forms. `add_pml_conditions` writes one `pml` condition per absorbing piece of the geometry (the pieces and their sides come from the `Pml` feature), so the geometry and the physics cannot disagree.

## Consequences

* A person or a host picks silicon, silica or sapphire by name; an example of a rotated sapphire block (r-plane, Bunge angles) is a project file.
* The numbers of the examples differ slightly from the old window's: the library values were checked against the literature (ADR 35) and are not the earlier rounded ones. The goldens of the physics crates are unaffected (they use inline numbers).
* The `silicon()` and `sapphire()` helpers of `femcore::material` stay for tests of other crates; no program uses them.

## Code

`crates/nyx-physics/src/{spec,physics,decode}.rs`, `crates/nyx-engine/src/{materials,meshing,pml}.rs`, `crates/femcore/src/material/spec.rs` (`Library::with_texts`), `crates/femcore/src/meshing/physics_size.rs`, `crates/nyx-{ems,sms}/src/lib.rs` (`sizing`), `crates/nyx-engine/tests/{materials,examples}.rs`.
decisions.title: The engine resolves named materials from the library and the project

# 59. The store knows nothing of a project: no femcore, no XML, the engine makes cards and metrics

Date: 2026-11-05

## Status

Accepted. Completes ADR 39 and resolves ROUGH_SPOTS R21 and R25 as the plan asked ("do not fix them in the old structure").

## Context

ADR 39 let the engine pass its own card function to `WorkflowDir`, but the store still parsed `nyx_project` XML through `femcore::xmlio`, made cards from the old `Project` shape and made run metrics from the old `SolveResult`.

## Decision

* `nyx-store` has no dependency on `femcore` or on any workspace crate. A spec is JSON text. `WorkflowDir::create`/`open` use `card::plain`, which reads only a `title`; programs that know projects pass `create_with`/`open_with` with `nyx_engine::store_link::card_of`. Run metrics are made by `nyx_engine::store_link::metrics_of`. `card::from_value`, `card::from_xml`, `runs::metrics_of` and the XML branch of path stripping (`strip_paths_xml`, which keeps its name, handles JSON) are deleted.
* The files keep their names (`experiment.nyx.xml`, `specs/<hash>.nyx.xml`) although they hold JSON; renaming them changes the `.nyx` archive whitelist and is the file-format decision of phase 8 (gate G6).
* No migration: workflows stored with XML specs do not open. This follows constraint 9 of the plan (no migration of old projects).
* `femcore` loses `xmlio` and the `quick-xml` dependency; the HDF5 writer (`h5io`, features `hdf5-metno` and `phdf5`) is deleted with the old result type it was written for.

## Consequences

* The dashboard cards of an engine workflow come from the engine's card (physics, study, wavelength, materials, parameters of the geometry).
* HDF5 results are not written by this build. The plan keeps HDF5 as an optional engine export; porting it to `nyx_physics::SolveResult` and the native mesh is a follow-up.

## Code

`crates/nyx-store/src/{card,flow,archive,runs}.rs`, `crates/nyx-engine/src/store_link.rs`.
decisions.title: The store knows nothing of a project: no femcore, no XML, the engine makes cards and metrics

# 6. One meshing interface: MeshPlan, with a simple and an adaptive mesher behind it

Date: 2026-11-02

## Status

Accepted (commit `a94dad3`, "Unified meshing interface").

## Context

Two ways of meshing a geom model existed: the constrained Delaunay mesher the app had always used (`geomdrive::mesh_geom_2d`) and the new metric adaptation of the mesher port. Callers (app, use cases, the MCP session) should not care which one made the cells, and names, selectors and boundary conditions must mean the same on either mesh.

## Decision

`meshing::mesh_model(list, &MeshPlan)` is the one way to mesh a geom model. `MeshPlan { opts, mesher }` chooses `Mesher::Simple` (chords of each geom edge, CDT, Ruppert refinement, lattice points in finer regions) or `Mesher::Adaptive(Adaptive { scale, grade, max_cells })` (the same start, then metric adaptation toward a size field built from the model: region sizes, `Size` rules, absorbing layers, edge curvature; graded). The result is a `MeshedGeom` with names, labels and exact geometry.

* Cell and facet labels are carried through unchanged by adaptation.
* Vertices that move or are created on a boundary or interface land on the **exact** geom edge (`GeomOracle2`), not on the chord polygon; vertices of the geometry never move.
* Adapting to an ungraded metric with sharp features is unreliable, so `grade` defaults to 0.4 and is always applied.
* `adapt_to_metrics` is the hook for an error estimator; a `MeshCache` gives warm starts and reuse across parameter sweeps (`154b64e`, tied to `geom::diff`).

## Consequences

* The app has a switch (`GeometrySpec::adapt_scale`) and a checkbox for physics sizing (`GeometrySpec::physics_sizing`, ADR 17).
* The 3D route (`physics_size::adapt_tets`, `pml3`, `estimate3`) has no app entry because there is no 3D geom mesh to adapt (extruded models do produce tets; the hook is not written).
* Mesh equality across the two meshers is only by names and exact geometry, not by cell count.

## Code

`crates/femcore/src/meshing.rs`, `meshing_pml.rs`, `geomdrive.rs`, `mesher.rs`, `meshers/adapt/{geom,field,drive,topo,ops}.rs`; `crates/app/src/state.rs`. History: `a94dad3`, `3fbb24d`, `154b64e`, `e69fefd`.

## Contract

`contracts/mesh` (labels survive adaptation) and `contracts/geom_model`.
decisions.title: One meshing interface: MeshPlan, with a simple and an adaptive mesher behind it

# 60. The examples are project files; the use cases are gone

Date: 2026-11-05

## Status

Accepted. Implements "the library contains no built-in devices or use cases; devices are `.nyx` files outside the program" (plan constraint 3) and the deletion of `usecases/` (plan phase 7).

## Context

The window opened with 18 projects built by code (`app/examples.rs`), two of which (the silicon-on-insulator wire and the Bragg grating) came from `femcore::usecases`, which the MCP session also called. Their geometry, materials and conditions lived in Rust, so changing an example meant recompiling, and the tests of other crates used the use cases as fixtures.

## Decision

* The examples are files, `examples/NN_name.nyx.json` at the repository root, found next to the program, in a parent folder of it or at `NYX_EXAMPLES` (`app/src/examples.rs`). They are written by `crates/nyx-engine/tests/make_examples.rs` (run it with `-- --ignored`), which builds each one **through engine commands** (`add_rect`, `add_overlay`, `add_physics`, `set_material`, `add_condition`, `add_pml_conditions`, ...), so an example is also a worked use of the interface. 16 examples: capacitor, cantilever, heated plate, thermal bar (heat feeding thermal expansion), block cantilever, WR-90 guide, loaded guide, sapphire cantilever (rotated crystal from the library), PML slab, plate with a hole, anchor loss (PML substrate), drilled plate, silicon strip on sapphire (optical and acoustic modes with PML, named materials), box cavity, SOI wire and its hybrid-mode variant.
* `crates/nyx-engine/tests/examples.rs` opens, checks, meshes and solves every example and compares the ones with a closed form (cantilever tip against Euler-Bernoulli, WR-90 cutoff, TE101 frequency of the box, the documented TE0 index of the SOI wire). These tests replace `usecases.rs`, `legacy_thermal.rs` and `legacy_contract.rs`.
* The two Bragg grating examples are not carried over: a swept layer with a `domain_offset` has domain numbers that carry no name, so a material cannot be assigned to them by name. Naming the domains of swept layers is open (a follow-up for the mesh owner).
* `femcore::testkit::soi` keeps the cross-section of the SOI wire as a fixture for the meshing and golden tests of other crates; `nyx-ems/tests/common` builds the typed problem from it.
* The benchmark programs (`bench`, `profile3d`, `mem_profile`, `cavity_bench`, `stage_log`, `eig_beam`) drive the physics through the `Physics` trait on generated meshes (`examples/common`); `complex_bench`, `soi_modes` and `bragg_gratings` are deleted with the use cases they studied.

## Consequences

* A change to an example is a regenerated file. The program ships with its `examples` and `materials` folders, not with devices in code.
* The window's New dialog and the start-from cards of the dashboard point at example files by position in the sorted list.

## Code

`examples/*.nyx.json`, `crates/nyx-engine/tests/{make_examples,examples}.rs`, `crates/nyx-engine/examples/*`, `crates/app/src/examples.rs`.
decisions.title: The examples are project files; the use cases are gone

# 61. Mesh convergence is an engine command

Date: 2026-11-05

## Status

Accepted. Replaces the `mesh_converge` check of the old session tools (ADR 15), which existed only for the silicon wire.

## Context

A number from a finite-element solve means little without a second mesh. The old `check_run` repeated a solve at 0.6 times the element sizes, but only for the SOI wire use case. After ADR 57 no tool can do it for a project of any physics.

## Decision

`convergence_check {physics, factor = 0.6, tolerance?}` solves the physics of the current project on a scratch engine, then on a project whose mesh is finer by `factor` (element size, adaptive size factor and chord deviation times `factor`, points per wavelength divided by it, the layers of a sweep with `1 / factor` times as many cells), and compares every eigenvalue (real and imaginary part), every value that orders the solutions and every numeric scalar. The reply has a row per quantity (coarse, refined, difference, relative difference, pass or fail when a tolerance was given), both cell counts and unknown counts, the worst relative difference and, with a tolerance, `converged`. The project, its mesh and its results are not changed. It is an expensive command (two solves).

## Consequences

* A host or the window can say whether a quoted number is converged for any physics; the guide cards tell a host to run it before quoting.
* The difference of two meshes is an indication, not an error bound; a smaller `factor` shows whether it is still falling.

## Code

`crates/nyx-engine/src/convergence.rs`, test `a_finer_mesh_confirms_or_refutes_a_number_through_convergence_check` in `crates/nyx-engine/tests/examples.rs`.
decisions.title: Mesh convergence is an engine command

# 62. Results and meshes are stored in HDF5; JSON is for small things

Date: 2026-11-05

## Status

Accepted on paul's instruction (HDF5 is central to how nyx stores the data of a solve). Restores the results file that phase 7 had dropped with the old result type (ADR 59 said it was a follow-up) and reverses the JSON fallback in the run record.

## Context

A solve produces fields with hundreds of thousands of values per solution and, for mode studies, complex fields per cell. As JSON text these are large, slow to write and parse, and lossy unless every digit is kept. The old `femcore::h5io` wrote them to HDF5; it was bound to the deleted `femcore::problem` types.

## Decision

* `nyx-engine::h5io` (cargo feature `hdf5`, off by default because it needs the HDF5 library at build time; set `HDF5_DIR`) writes **the project, the mesh and the latest result of every solved physics** (all solutions, all fields with their components and units, the per-cell fields, scalars and the stage log) into one file, chunked and deflate-compressed, and reads it back **bit for bit** (test `tests/h5.rs`). Layout version 3 is documented in the module and listed in `VERSIONS.md` (`results_file`). The parallel (MPI-IO) writer is not ported.
* Commands `export_results {path}` and `results_file_info {path}`; a build without the feature answers them with "unsupported", so a host can tell.
* **Every recorded run keeps `results.h5`** in its run folder when the feature is on (engine runs, MCP runs and the window's runs); no JSON copy of the fields is written in that case. Without the feature the engine falls back to `result_<physics>.json`, which is larger; builds that care about size or speed use the feature.
* Measured on two examples, the HDF5 file including the mesh and the project is 2.5 to 2.9 times smaller than the JSON of the result alone (SOI wire 487 kB against 1243 kB; thermal bar 413 kB against 1167 kB).
* **XDMF** (`nyx-engine::xdmf`, recovered from the old writer, XML written with `quick-xml`): next to every `.h5` that `export_results` writes and in every recorded run (`results.xdmf`), a description that names the nodes, cells and fields under `/viz/<physics>`; a scalar field is a hard link to the stored dataset, a vector field has a three-component copy. Each physics is a collection of grids, one per solution. A test resolves every reference against the file. *Amended by ADR 99 (layout 4): there is no `/viz` group any more. The XDMF is the light index of the results as stored, for nyx and its tools only (not for ParaView), and names `/results/<physics>/points`, `cells` (in nyx's cell node order, stated in `CellNodeOrder`) and `solution_k/fields/<name>`, vectors with their stored components.*
* Project and spec files, run records and the workflow manifests stay small JSON text. Whether the project file should be XML after all is open with paul (it was JSON by plan constraint 11).

## Consequences

* The window's "Open results file" is not back yet; `results_file_info` and `read_results` exist for it.
* Making `hdf5` a default feature would make the library a build requirement for every developer; that is a decision for paul.

## Code

`crates/nyx-engine/src/{h5io,xdmf,results_file,store_link}.rs`, `crates/nyx-engine/tests/h5.rs`, `crates/app/src/shell.rs`.
decisions.title: Results and meshes are stored in HDF5; JSON is for small things

# 63. One `format` key, JSON for small files, HDF5 for bulk data

Date: 2026-11-12

## Status

Accepted by the plan (phase 8) and by paul's storage decision of 2026-11-05 (HDF5 is central; project and spec files stay small JSON; no bulk data as JSON). Replaces the provisional layout of the project file and the `engine_project` exemplar (ADR 37 named it provisional); completes ADR 62.

## Context

Until phase 8 the saved layout was provisional: no file said which layout it was. Spec files were still called `experiment.nyx.xml` and `specs/<hash>.nyx.xml` although they have held JSON since phase 7 (the XML project format is gone with `xmlio`), `nyx-store` had a function `strip_paths_xml` that parsed JSON, and a build without HDF5 wrote the fields of a result as `result_<physics>.json`.

## Decision

* **`format` key, first value 1, written once at three levels:** `Project` (`nyx-engine`, `PROJECT_FORMAT`), `FeatureList` (`geom::model::FORMAT`) and `ProblemSpec` (`nyx_physics::PROBLEM_FORMAT`). The three are separate because each is also read alone: a feature list by `set_geometry` and the geom goldens, a problem by `set_problem` and the physics contracts. A value other than 1 is refused with a plain message by `FeatureList::validate`, `validate_spec` and `Project::check_formats`.
* **No migration code.** `Project::from_json` (the file boundary) requires the key in the project, in its geometry and in every problem; a file of the earlier layout is refused with a message that names the missing key and says older files are not converted. A command that is given a problem or feature list *without* the key (an MCP call, a test) reads it as the current format; only files are strict. The last commit that wrote the old layout is tagged `last-old-format` (74851193).
* **Spec files are JSON by name.** `experiment.nyx.json`, `specs/<hash>.nyx.json`, `strip_paths` (was `strip_paths_xml`). The `nyx` archive accepts exactly these names. There is no XML code left in the workspace except the XDMF *description* file written next to HDF5 results (ADR 62), which is XML by the XDMF specification and is output only. The project and spec files are not XML.
* **No bulk data as JSON.** `result_<physics>.json` is gone. A recorded run keeps `results.h5` (+ `results.xdmf`) in a build with feature `hdf5`; a build without it records the metrics and the log only, and says so in `log.txt`. Run records, `workflow.json`, `history.jsonl`, specs, material files and descriptors stay small text. Golden files of tests are inputs and oracles, not stored results.
* **Contract exemplars.** `engine_project.v2.json` (was `.v1.`, provisional) and `problem_spec.v3.json` (was `.v2.`) carry the key; the old files are removed (`VERSIONS.md`). `store_workflow` and `store_run` do not change: the store holds spec text and a hash and does not know the layout (ADR 59). The golden feature lists of `geom` and the 16 example projects were rewritten with the key and nothing else; the numbers in `*.expected.json` are untouched.

## Consequences

* A later change of layout bumps the number, adds a reader or a refusal in one place and a `.v<n+1>.` exemplar.
* Project files written before phase 8 (the examples of phase 7, a saved workspace) do not open. They are regenerated (`make_examples`) or re-saved from a window built before; there is no converter.
* **`hdf5` is a default feature of `nyx-engine`** (paul, 2026-11-12), so the app, the MCP server and every test build have it; `.cargo/config.toml` sets `HDF5_DIR` for the development machine (an environment value wins) and the HDF5 DLL must be on PATH at run time. `--no-default-features --features dfs,sms,ems` builds without it, and a run then stores no fields.
* **The window opens a results file** (paul, 2026-11-12; done): engine command `open_results` reads the file, makes its project the project, meshes it again (meshing is deterministic, ADR 55) and refuses the file when that mesh is not the stored one, then takes the stored results as the latest results. The window offers it in the Open dialog (`.h5`) and on drop, and shows the results at once.
* **The MPI-IO writer is ported** (paul, 2026-11-12, for future GPU and multicore use): `nyx-engine::h5io` writes through an `Io` that holds the process's `Partition` (rank and size); every process makes the same collective group, attribute and dataset creations and writes only its own block of rows (`Partition::rows`), so a parallel file reads back as the serial one. `export_results` takes `parallel`. The MPI-IO driver and `mpi-sys` are behind the cargo feature `phdf5` (needs an MPI-enabled HDF5 library and an MPI SDK; no MPI code is compiled without it). **Not run here:** this machine has no MPI SDK or parallel HDF5, so the `phdf5` code is written to the old, working design but not compiled; the partition logic is tested by emulating three processes against one file (`h5io` unit tests). XDMF stays the XML side, the project file stays JSON.

## Code

`crates/geom/src/model.rs`, `crates/nyx-physics/src/{spec,validate}.rs`, `crates/nyx-engine/src/{project,store_link}.rs`, `crates/nyx-engine/tests/format.rs`, `crates/nyx-store/src/{flow,archive}.rs`, `docs/architecture/contracts/{engine_project.v2,problem_spec.v3}.json`.
decisions.title: One `format` key, JSON for small files, HDF5 for bulk data

# 64. Identity: one persisted hash (BLAKE3 of the bytes); every other hash is a cache key

Date: 2026-11-13

## Status

Accepted (phase 9). Resolves ROUGH_SPOTS R08 ("three hash functions, none documented as the identity rule"). `nyx-session` and its FNV handles are gone (ADR 57), which leaves the two kinds below.

## Context

Hashes are used for two different jobs. One is *identity*: two things with the same hash are the same thing, and the hash is written to disk or compared across runs and machines (a frozen spec, a run's spec, an archive entry). The other is a *cache key*: a hash decides whether a computed value in memory is still valid and never leaves the process.

## Decision

* **Identity is `nyx_store::util::hash_bytes`**: the text `b3:` and the first 32 hex digits of the BLAKE3 hash of the bytes. It is the only hash that is persisted or compared across processes: the content address of a frozen spec (`specs/<hash>.nyx.json`), the spec of a version and of a run (`spec_hash`), the check of every entry of a `nyx` archive. The bytes are the text a project serialises to with sorted keys (`Project::to_json`, ADR 26), so the same project has the same hash in every build. A change of the file format (ADR 63) changes the hashes; that is intended, nothing migrates.
* **Cache keys may use any hash but are never stored or sent.** The engine keys its mesh and its results by `hash_bytes` of the geometry, mesh settings and sizing (`Engine::mesh_key`) and of the whole project (`Engine::stamp`), so an edit never has to remember to invalidate them. `geom::math::Hasher64` (64-bit, over the numeric value of each expression, the operation and the name) decides which features of an evaluated model changed (`geom::diff`, the arrangement cache); its numbers are meaningless outside the process and must never be written to a file or put in a contract. `femcore::adapt::topo::FxHasher` is a hash-map hasher, not an identity.
* **Run and workflow ids are not hashes**: they are short time-ordered random ids (`util::short_id`).
* A new persisted identity uses `hash_bytes`. A new cache key may use what is convenient, and says so in a comment.

## Consequences

* Nothing to unify: `geom` stays free of a hash dependency (R18, `tests/layering.rs`), the store keeps BLAKE3.
* Two projects that differ only in the order of keys or in white space are the same project after `to_json`; two that differ in one digit are different.

## Code

`crates/nyx-store/src/util.rs` (`hash_bytes`, `short_id`), `crates/nyx-engine/src/engine.rs` (`mesh_key`, `stamp`), `crates/geom/src/math.rs` (`Hasher64`), `crates/geom/src/diff.rs`.
decisions.title: Identity: one persisted hash (BLAKE3 of the bytes); every other hash is a cache key
