# 65. Closing the restructure: what the final structure replaces, and the rules left

Date: 2026-11-13

## Status

Accepted (phase 9). Brings the older records in line with the code after phases 1 to 8. Supersedes ADR 4, ADR 22 and ADR 23, and supersedes ADR 15 and ADR 14 in part. It decides R23 (formatting, lints) and R14 (stale design notes).

## Context

The decision records of 2026-10-28 to 2026-11-03 describe the structure *before* the restructure. Several are now wrong in what they tell a reader to do, even though they were right when written.

## Decision

**Superseded or amended.**
* **ADR 4 (SimplexMesh is the one mesh the kernels read): superseded** by ADR 5 and ADR 32 and by the physics interface of ADR 25. `Physics::solve` takes the exchange mesh `femcore::mesh::Mesh`; a kernel numbers its own unknowns with `nyx_physics::discretise` (the old `SimplexMesh` numbering lives on as that discretisation and as the view the window and the results file draw on).
* **ADR 5 (native mixed-cell mesh)** is no longer "not implemented on the solver side": the mesh is native from the mesher to the physics interface (ADR 32) and the structured layers are native (ADR 52).
* **ADR 8** was superseded by ADR 33 (phase 3). **ADR 14 (workflow store)** stays in force for the folder layout and the archives; the spec files are `experiment.nyx.json` and `specs/<hash>.nyx.json` (ADR 63), the store takes spec text and a card function (ADR 39) and knows nothing of a project (ADR 59). **ADR 15** (AI interface in its own workspace) is superseded in part by ADR 26 (one workspace), ADR 28 (one `nyx-connect`) and ADR 57 (the MCP tools are the engine commands; `nyx-session` is dissolved); the MCP server itself and the host connection stand.
* **ADR 22 (use cases and chips live in femcore): superseded** by ADR 24 (chips and Brillouin removed) and ADR 60 (examples are project files; the use cases are gone).
* **ADR 23 (the app is a thin shell over one project): superseded** by ADR 57: the project and every action live in `nyx-engine`; the window and the MCP server are front-ends of one `Engine`.

**Formatting and lints (R23).**
* `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets` is clean. Where a lint is allowed on purpose it is allowed on the item or the module with a reason (`type_complexity` for local tuples of per-cell arrays, `large_enum_variant` for `Stiffness`, which is made once per material).
* `rustfmt` is applied to the crates that already follow `geom`'s settings (`geom`, `nyx-physics`, `nyx-dfs`, `nyx-sms`, `nyx-ems`, `nyx-analysis`, `nyx-engine`) and to nothing else. `femcore`, `nyx-store`, `nyx-mcp`, `nyx-connect` and `app` stay as written: formatting them would rewrite most of their lines (and the line endings of the older files, which are CRLF) for no change in behaviour, and would bury the history that `jj` and `git blame` are used for. New files in those crates follow the style around them.
* `rust-version` in the manifest is 1.99, the toolchain the code is built and tested with (`rust-toolchain.toml`); the old "1.84" was never tested.

**Records.** The design notes of the time before the restructure (`GEOMETRY_ARCHITECTURE.md`, `GEOM_HANDOFF.md`, `SWEEP_CACHING_PROPOSAL.md`, `WORKFLOWS_DESIGN.md`, `MCP_ASSISTANT_PLAN.md`, `KERNEL_PORT_STATUS.md` and others) are history and are not rewritten (R14). The place to find what is true now is `docs/architecture/` (ADRs, `workspace.dsl`, contracts) and `CLAUDE.md`.

**Parked, as paul asked ("we will see at the very end"):** run-time plug-ins, two-way coupling, Brillouin as an optional physics crate (tag `sbs-last`), and the licence check of the BSD-2-Clause ports against nyx's own licence before anything is published.

## Consequences

* A reader who follows an ADR marked superseded is sent to the one that replaced it.
* The guards that keep the final structure are tests: `tests/layering.rs` (crate layering, and geom's dependencies: R18), `femcore/tests/expr_grammar.rs` (R06), the contract suites (ADR 19) and `check_code_to_adr.sh`.

## Code

`docs/architecture/` (this directory, `workspace.dsl`, `diagrams.md`, `CODE_TO_ADR.md`), `CLAUDE.md`, `Cargo.toml` (`rust-version`).
decisions.title: Closing the restructure: what the final structure replaces, and the rules left

# 66. A swept section can be a periodic cell: sorted vertices and `fill` layers

Date: 2026-11-14

## Status

Accepted (benchmark A3, bookmark `restructure-10-a3-snowflake`). Extends the sweep of ADR 54 and the engine mesher of ADR 57; uses the Floquet pairs of ADR 25.

## Context

A photonic or phononic crystal slab is a periodic cell patterned in the plane of the wafer, with the slab thickness and, for light, a layer of cladding above and below it. In nyx the only way to a 3D cell with Floquet walls that works is a 2D section swept along the surface normal, because the 3D lattice mesher fits curved and slanted walls only to order `alpha h` and does not make opposite faces congruent (`no vertex on the destination boundary matches ...`).

Two things were missing for a slab with a pattern.

1. `extrude_y` cuts each prism into tetrahedra along the vertex numbers. Opposite walls of a periodic section then are cut differently unless the vertices are numbered by their coordinates; `geomdrive::sort_nodes` does that, and the engine mesher did not call it for a sweep.
2. A sweep layer takes the section's domain numbers (plus an offset). A cladding layer above a slab with holes would be partly Si and partly air, so the cladding could not be a layer of air.

## Decision

* `SweepLayer` (project) and `mesher::Layer` (femcore) gain `fill`, a region name (`Option<String>` in the project, the domain number in femcore): every cell of the layer belongs to that region, whatever the region of the section; the domain offset is then not used. An unknown name is refused with the list of regions.
* The engine mesher numbers the section's vertices by coordinates (`sort_nodes`) before it sweeps, so the walls of a periodic section pair. Meshes of swept models that were not periodic change only in their vertex order.
* `set_mesh` takes `fill` in a `sweep` layer (`engine_commands` 1.6, additive).

## Not done

* A primitive hexagonal (rhombic) cell does not work: the 2D mesher leaves degenerate (sub-nanometre) boundary facets on slanted edges, so the two slanted walls cannot be paired. The benchmark uses the rectangular two-site supercell instead (the bands are folded once). Fixing the 2D mesher for slanted periodic walls is recorded in `ROUGH_SPOTS.md`.
* The 3D meshers (lattice, Rivara) still do not pair periodic faces.

## Consequences

* A slab-with-holes cell with cladding is a section, a sweep of `[slab, air, air]` layers (or `[air, slab, air]`), and a pair of Floquet conditions on the section walls; the same project gives the photonic (`ems` cavity) and the phononic (`sms`, air inactive) band structure.
* The vertex renumbering is a pure permutation: results do not change beyond rounding.

## Code

`crates/femcore/src/meshing/mesher.rs` (`Layer::fill`), `crates/nyx-engine/src/meshing.rs`, `crates/nyx-engine/src/project.rs` (`SweepLayer`), tests `a_fill_layer_gives_all_its_cells_one_domain` (`crates/femcore/tests/meshing.rs`) and `crates/nyx-engine/tests/swept_cell.rs` (a vacuum cell with a closed form, and the refusal of a fill that names no region).
decisions.title: A swept section can be a periodic cell: sorted vertices and `fill` layers

# 67. `pmc`: a magnetic wall for `ems` cavities and Floquet cells

Date: 2026-11-14

## Status

Accepted (benchmark A3, bookmark `restructure-10-a3-snowflake`). Extends the cavity kernel of ADR 45.

## Context

The `ems` cavity study puts a perfect electric conductor on every exterior boundary that is not a Floquet face (ADR 45: "Outer walls not otherwise described are perfect electric conductors"). A slab with a mirror plane at its mid-plane has two parity classes. The TE-like modes of a photonic crystal slab, the ones the literature calls the even modes, have the tangential electric field even under the reflection, so the mirror plane is a perfect magnetic conductor for them. With only PEC walls the even modes cannot be isolated, and the cell has twice the volume it needs.

A magnetic wall is the natural condition of the curl-curl form: nothing is constrained on it.

## Decision

* `ems` has a boundary condition `pmc` ("Magnetic wall (mirror plane)", no parameters, cavity study only). The facets with its boundary numbers are left out of the PEC set of the cavity kernel; the edge dofs and the nodal gradient space on them are free, as inside the domain.
* `Problem` gains `pmc: Vec<i32>`; `decode` fills it and refuses the condition outside the cavity study.
* `physics_ems` descriptors 1.2 (additive).

## Consequences

* A mirror plane halves the cell and selects the even modes: checked against the closed form of a box whose upper wall is magnetic (`a_magnetic_wall_is_the_mirror_plane_of_the_doubled_box`, the modes of the doubled PEC box with `sin(p pi z / 2d)`, p odd).
* The odd modes need the mirror plane electric: that is the default, so they are the same project with `pmc` removed on the half cell.
* `sms` has no such condition: a mirror plane for the solid is a fixed normal displacement (`fixed` with the component that is normal).

## Code

`crates/nyx-ems/src/problem.rs`, `crates/nyx-ems/src/cavity.rs` (`assemble_emw_eigen`), `crates/nyx-ems/src/lib.rs` (`bc_kinds`), test in `crates/nyx-ems/tests/emw3d.rs`.
decisions.title: `pmc`: a magnetic wall for `ems` cavities and Floquet cells

# 68. The axisymmetric solid gets a study

Date: 2026-11-14

## Status

Proposed (capability R6, the merge of the three workstreams on `capability-r6-sms-axisym`). Amends ADR 43: the library entry stays, the study is added. The axis conditions and the cylindrical stretch of the kernel are ADR 69. Numbered 68 because the A3 branch (`restructure-10-a3-snowflake`) already holds ADR 66 and 67.

## Context

Benchmark A1 (Bindel and Govindjee 2005, a disk on a post anchored in a substrate) was blocked on "no axisymmetric `sms`". The kernel exists and is tested (ADR 43: `solve_solid_axisym`, ring closed forms, crystal-ring frame checks), but it was a library function: `Sms::studies()` listed `static` and `eigenfrequency` only, and `run` always called `solve_solid`. ADR 43 left the study to the owner of the window ("nothing needs it before phase 7"); `CAPABILITY_PLAN.md` R6 and the A1 report ask for it, and paul stated that the support exists and only needs wiring. `nyx-ems` is the precedent (ADR 46: study `axisymmetric_modes`).

Everything downstream is generic: `nyx-engine` never names a physics, `set_study` takes any kind the descriptors list, `add_pml` plus `add_pml_conditions` write `x`/`z` layers of a 2D model, the window draws the Study tab from the descriptors, and the MCP tools are the engine commands (ADR 57). So the change is inside `nyx-sms` and the contracts of `sms`.

## Decision

A study of `sms`, parallel to the `axisymmetric_modes` study of `ems`.

* **The study.** `kind` `axisymmetric_eigenfrequency`, name "Axisymmetric eigenfrequencies", `Dims::Two`, parameters `n_modes` (integer, default 6, min 1), `f_search` (Hz, default 0 = lowest modes, range >= 0) and `azimuthal_order` (integer `m`, range -100000 to 100000, same wording and range as `ems`; the displacement goes as `exp(-j m theta)`, `m > 0` runs along +y). The mesh is the (r, z) half plane with `x = r`; the displacement components are `ux` radial, `uz` axial, `uy` azimuthal (the order of `fixed`).
* **The typed problem.** `Study::AxisymmetricEigenfrequency { n_modes, f_search, azimuthal_order: i64 }`; `Study::kind()` returns the string, `Study::is_eigen()` is true for it, `decode` reads it, `check_finite` covers `f_search`.
* **What the study refuses** (`Problem::check_axisymmetric`, called by `decode` and by `run`, so the typed problem is held to the same rules as the envelope): a mesh that is not 2D (`Sms::validate` and `run`); a mesh with a point at `x < -1e-9` of its width ("the (r, z) half plane must lie in x >= 0", `solve_axisymmetric`); a boundary load; a Floquet-periodic pair (no translation to repeat); a low-reflecting boundary, with code `unsupported`, because `lrb::damping_matrix` has no `r` weight (rough spot D1: the damping of the axisymmetric kernel is wrong today and is not made reachable through a new door); a layer along `y` (`check_wafer`) or with `x = minus` ("a layer cannot absorb towards the axis"); a fixed value other than zero. Absorbing layers (`pml` with `x = plus` and `z`) are allowed.
* **What it ignores.** `plane`, `thickness`, `thermal` and `solver` are not read; when a non-default `plane` or `thickness` is present the log says so. `inactive` is honoured. `Sms::sizing` treats the new kind like `eigenfrequency` (a wavelength per region from `f_search`), and `Sms::fields` lists `|u|`, `Re ux`, `Re uz`, `Re uy`, `|uy|`.
* **The result.** One `Solution` per mode sorted by `Re f`; `value = Re f` (Hz) and **`eigenvalue = [Re f, Im f]`** on every mode (also without layers, where `Im f` is rounding noise of the complex solver, below 1e-8 of `Re f` in the test). Node fields `|u|`, `Re ux`, `Re uz`, `Re uy`, `|uy|` (phase rotated so the largest component is real, unit maximum). Cell fields are the complex `ux`, `uz`, `uy` as before. Scalars per mode `N`: `fN (Hz)` (a number when lossless, the text `re +imi` when lossy), `QN = Re f / (2 |Im f|)` when lossy, and **`layer fraction N`**, the share of `int rho |u|^2 r` that lies in absorbing layers (0 without layers; from the real mass weights `rho r` of the layer cells, not from the stretched ones). It lets a host or a test tell a resonator mode from a layer mode, the complaint of findings A1 and A4. The kernel gives `Im f > 0` for the layers of `sms` (measured in `tests/axisym_study.rs`); the study doc says so.
* **Names (rough spot D2).** The node fields of the shared stage `cross_section_fields` were `ux`, `uz`, `uy` although they are real parts of complex modes; they are now `Re ux`, `Re uz`, `Re uy`, as the 2D PML kernel and `nyx-ems` name them (contract `kernel_stages` 1.4 says so). The per-cell complex fields keep their names.
* **Entries.** `cross_section::solve_axisymmetric(mesh, problem)` is the study's entry (the name `nyx-ems` uses); `solve_solid_axisym(mesh, problem, m)` stays for the ring tests. `assemble_cross_section` accepts both `Study::Eigenfrequency` (with `m` from the argument) and the new study. `run` dispatches on the study; `solve_solid` forwards the new study to `solve_axisymmetric`.
* The `Physics` trait, `ProblemSpec`, `SolveResult`, the registry and the engine commands do not change shape (`physics_api` stays 1.1).

## Consequences

* The study is reachable from the envelope, the engine, the window (Study tab) and MCP with no change outside `nyx-sms`; example project and MCP proof are the engine step of the plan.
* A body that touches the axis is solved with the regularity conditions of ADR 69 and its layers are the cylindrical stretch of ADR 69, so a disk on a post on a substrate is a model of this study (engine example 17, the MCP proof). The study's own mesh rule stays `x >= 0`.
* Not covered, and recorded: the low-reflecting boundary with `r` weight (D1), the azimuthal tie at `m = +-1` on the axis, a complex shift (`f_search` stays real, enough for Q of 1e3 to 1e5), the `periodic` Floquet pair.
* Contracts: `physics_sms` 1.3 (additive: the study and its fields), `physics_sms_result` 1.1 (additive: the shapes `axisymmetric_eigenfrequency` and `axisymmetric_eigenfrequency_pml`), `kernel_stages` 1.4 (additive, with the rename of D2).

## What was verified

`crates/nyx-sms/tests/axisym_study.rs`: on a solid disk that touches the axis the study gives the contour mode of the closed form to 2.4e-5; the engine example `17_disk_anchor_loss` solves through engine commands (test T10), `convergence_check` compares the complex eigenvalues (T11) and the MCP server over stdio describes the study and returns `Q1` for the same model (T12); the envelope (`Sms::solve` of a `ProblemSpec`), the typed problem (`nyx_sms::run`) and the library entry (`solve_solid_axisym` with the same `m`) give identical frequencies at `m = 0` and `m = 2`; the refusals above each fail with their own message and a good problem passes; an absorbing layer on the outer part of a ring section gives complex frequencies with `Q = Re f / (2 |Im f|)` and layer fractions between 0 and 1 (0.79 to 0.96 for the four lowest modes of the test ring); descriptors, fields and sizing. `stages.rs` checks that the stages compose to `solve_axisymmetric`, `determinism.rs` that two runs give the same bits (a layer, `m = 1`), `cancel_and_log.rs` the stage log and `cancelled`, `contracts.rs` the descriptors exemplar, the result-shape exemplar (two new entries) and an example spec of the new kind.

## What was not verified

The quality factor of a model that matches a published anchor-loss number (benchmark A1 is a later step: `crates/nyx-engine/tests/benchmark_a1.rs` is an ignored skeleton until paul has agreed the material and the criteria); the sign convention of `Im f` is observed, not derived; the window's Study tab was not looked at (it follows from `forms.rs` being descriptor-driven, ADR 57).

## Code

`crates/nyx-sms/src/{problem,lib,cross_section,solid}.rs`, `crates/nyx-sms/tests/{axisym_study,stages,contracts,determinism,cancel_and_log}.rs`, `crates/nyx-engine/tests/{examples,make_examples,benchmark_a1}.rs`, `crates/nyx-mcp/tests/stdio.rs`, `examples/17_disk_anchor_loss.nyx.json`, `docs/architecture/contracts/{physics_sms,physics_sms_result}.v1.json`, `docs/architecture/contracts/VERSIONS.md`.

## Contract

`physics_sms` 1.3, `physics_sms_result` 1.1, `kernel_stages` 1.4.

# 69. Axis conditions and the cylindrical stretch of the axisymmetric solid kernel

Date: 2026-11-14

## Status

Proposed (capability R6, the merge of the three workstreams: K1 axis conditions on `capability-r6-sms-axis`, K2 cylindrical stretch on `capability-r6-sms-pml`, joined on `capability-r6-sms-axisym`). Amends ADR 43 ("a mesh that touches the axis is refused as before" no longer holds, and the layers of the axisymmetric solid are now the cylindrical stretch). ADR 68 is the study that reaches this kernel. Numbered 69 because the A3 branch (`restructure-10-a3-snowflake`) already holds ADR 66 and 67. Plan: `SMS_AXISYM_PLAN.md` sections 4.3 and 8.

## Context

**Axis (K1).** Benchmark A1 (a disk on a post on a substrate) has bodies that touch the axis `r = 0`. ADR 43 refused such a mesh. The refusal was a check `r <= 0` at a quadrature point, which the interior quadrature rules (`quad_rule`: three points of degree 2, six of degree 4, none on an edge) can only fail on a degenerate cell, so assembly already ran on a mesh that touches the axis. What was missing is the regularity of `u(r, z) exp(-i m theta)` at `r = 0`: without essential conditions on the axis dofs the `1/r` terms of the energy act only as a penalty and a mode may carry a spurious displacement on the axis.

**Absorbing layers (K2).** `nyx_sms::axisym` assembled the absorbing layers of the axisymmetric solid with the stretches `s_r` and `s_z` only: the gradients were divided by them and the cell integral multiplied by `s_r s_z`, but the `1/r` terms of the strains (`e_tt`, `g_zt`, `g_rt`, the `m / r` terms) and the weight `r` kept the real radius. In a layer that stretches `r` this is not the analytic continuation of the equations, so the layer is not perfectly matched in the cylindrical case (finding G2 of the plan). The electromagnetic kernel does it right (`AxiMaterial::with_pml` in `nyx-ems/src/axisym.rs`, ADR 46: `r~` and `s_theta = r~ / r`). The solid kernel had no layer test at all before this one.

## Decision (K1): the axis

* The axis dofs are the dofs (vertices and P2 edge midpoints) with `r <= 1e-9` of the extent of the mesh (`axisym::axis_tolerance`). `axisym::axis_constraints` returns the components to hold at zero and `assemble_cross_section` adds them to the fixed set before the reduction, so a boundary condition and an axis condition on one dof are the same dof held once.
* Derivation: finiteness at `r -> 0` of `e_tt = (u_r - i m u_t) / r`, `g_zt = du_t/dz - i m u_z / r` and `g_rt = du_t/dr - u_t / r - i m u_r / r` gives `u_r = i m u_t`, `u_z = 0` for `m != 0`, and then `(1 - m^2) u_t = 0` from `g_rt`:

  | `m` | held at zero on the axis |
  |---|---|
  | 0 | `u_r`, `u_theta` (`u_z` free) |
  | +-1 | `u_z`; `u_r` and `u_theta` stay free (the tie `u_r = i m u_theta` is not imposed, `ROUGH_SPOTS.md` R6a) |
  | \|m\| >= 2 | all three |

* An azimuthal order that is not an integer is refused when the mesh touches the axis (a single-valued displacement has an integer order). A mesh with a vertex at `r < -1e-9` of its extent is refused by cell; so is a cell whose three vertices lie on the axis (no area). Meshes off the axis are untouched: no existing number changes (`ring_model_axes` golden, `axisym_closed_form.rs`, `ring_frame.rs` pass unchanged).
* The log of the result says which components were held on how many axis dofs.
* **Shared function signature touched:** `CrossAssembly` gains the public field `axis_dofs: usize`. Nothing else in the public stage API changes.

## Decision (K2): the cylindrical stretch

1. **Same stretch as the EM kernel.** Inside a layer whose `x` direction (the radial one) is stretched, the radius becomes the complex `r~ = int s_r dr` counted from the interface of the layer. With `s_theta = r~ / r` every `1/r` of the strains becomes `1/(s_theta r)` and the weight `r dr dz` becomes `s_theta r s_r s_z dr dz`; in the mass the weight `r` becomes `s_theta r` and the determinant is `s_r s_z s_theta`. `s_z` and `s_r` on the gradients stay.
2. **Where.** `nyx_sms::axisym::cylindrical_stretches(mesh, pml)` returns `[s_r, s_z, s_theta]` per cell: the first two from `femcore::pml::cell_stretches`, the third from `femcore::pml::radial_coordinate` at the cell centre (the integral of the profile, exactly the formula that was inline in `AxiMaterial::with_pml`; moved to femcore as a pure move, `nyx-ems` now calls it, its numbers are unchanged). `assemble_stiffness_axisym` and `assemble_mass_axisym` keep their signatures and read the third component of the stretch they are given (`None` is the unstretched ring); `assemble_cross_section` builds the stretch with `cylindrical_stretches`. A cell outside a layer with a radial stretch has `s_theta = 1` exactly, so every model without such a layer assembles to the same matrices as before.
3. **The test function is not conjugated in the stretch.** The weak form is the analytic continuation of `int conj(eps(v)) : D : eps(u) r dA` in which the conjugation reverses the phase `exp(-i m theta)` of the test function and nothing else. So inside a layer the `m / r` terms of the test side are `+i m / (s_theta r)`, not the conjugate of the trial side's `-i m / (s_theta r)` (that would conjugate `s_theta`). The code uses `beta_h = i m / (s_theta r)`; for `s_theta = 1` it is the old `conj(beta)`. The matrices are complex symmetric inside a layer, as the 2D PML kernel's already are, and the shift-and-invert eigensolve is the one the PML kernel uses.
4. **`s_theta` is the value at the cell centre, as in the EM kernel.** In a layer `r~(r)` is therefore `(r~_c / r_c) r` inside a cell, not exactly the radial integral: the error is of order `h / r` per cell and falls with the mesh (measured below). Evaluating `s_theta` at the quadrature points would remove it; not done so that the two kernels read alike (plan step 4).

## The deliberate difference from Bindel and Govindjee

As the plan reads the paper (Bindel and Govindjee, their Sec. 3, after the weak form), the Jacobian factor `r` of the axisymmetric case "should not be transformed": the layer stretches the derivatives and the `1/r` of the strains are left to the real radius, which is what nyx did before this change. K2 uses the analytic continuation `r -> r~` (Collino and Monk; the EM kernel's choice) because it is the perfectly matched form for the cylindrical wave equation: the plan expects the two to differ by a reflection at the layer interface of order `lambda / r`. I did not have the paper at hand while writing this; the quotation is the plan's. If paul prefers the paper's form it is one change (`s_theta = 1`), which the T6 test of this file already does through the public stage pieces; no flag was added.

T6 (`tests/axisym_pml.rs`) measures what it makes, on a thin annular wheel on a ring-shaped post on a substrate, absorbing layers left, right and below, order-2 profile, `m = 0`, wheel mode near `f = 0.086` (units `E = rho = 1`, `nu = 0.3`; the wheel sits at `r` 12 to 16, the layers at `r` 2 to 8 and 20 to 26):

| wheel, layers | `Q`, `s_theta = r~ / r` | `Q`, `s_theta = 1` | relative difference |
|---|---|---|---|
| `r` 12 to 16, thickness 3, strength 3 | 121.84 | 122.38 | 4.5e-3 |
| `r` 12 to 16, thickness 6, strength 3 | 122.18 | 121.95 | 1.9e-3 |
| `r` 9 to 13, thickness 3, strength 3 | 76.90 | 77.55 | 8.4e-3 |
| `r` 9 to 13, thickness 3, strength 6 | 77.15 | 78.13 | 1.3e-2 |

So on this model the two forms agree to about 1 %, more where the layers are nearer the axis, and the difference is of the order of the insensitivity to the layer itself (next section), not larger. The standard candle A1 has the disk and its layers nearer the axis and a different wave-length to radius ratio; its report must state which form was used and may repeat T6 on it.

## Consequences

* Solid disks, posts and substrates can be solved; the radial contour modes of a thin disk now have a closed-form check.
* For `m = +-1` the axis is regular only in the weak sense (the tie is a penalty); rigid translation and tilt, which satisfy it exactly, come out at zero frequency.

## What was verified

**K1, the axis.** Tests `crates/nyx-sms/tests/axisym_axis.rs` (second-order elements; the printed errors are the measured ones, see the status section of `docs/RESTRUCTURE_STATUS.md`): T1 torsion of a free solid cylinder (`u_theta = J1(kr)`, zeros of `J2`), T2 radial plane-strain modes with `u_z = 0` on the ends (`u_r = J1(kr)`, `k R J0 / J1 = (1 - 2 nu) / (1 - nu)`), T3 the radial contour modes of a thin disk (`lambda J0 / J1 = 1 - nu`) and `m = 2` stability under refinement, plus `m = 1` rigid modes and the refusal of a mesh that crosses the axis.

**K2, the stretch.**

All numbers are printed by `crates/nyx-sms/tests/axisym_pml.rs` (`-- --nocapture`), second-order elements; T4 to T6 use off-axis meshes, T5b and T6b the topology of A1 (all touching the axis). Units `E = rho = 1`, `nu = 0.3` unless said.

* **Unit stretch changes nothing** (T4a): a layer with strength 0 and `re = 1` on a ring gives the unstretched frequencies to 1e-9 at `m = 0` and 2. All pre-existing sms and ems tests pass unchanged (the old numbers are bit-for-bit as far as the tests can see: no golden was touched, `ring_model_axes` included).
* **A real radial stretch is the longer ring** (T4b): `re = 1.5` on a ring of width 0.3 at `r = 1` gives the frequencies of the ring of width 0.45, `m = 0` and 3, worst relative error 1.1e-2, 7.2e-4, 3.0e-4 for 6 x 2, 12 x 4 and 24 x 8 cells. This is the per-cell `s_theta` of decision 4: it falls with the mesh and is an upper bound for the effect at a real layer.
* **Large radius** (T4): a clamped strip `r` in `[R0, R0 + L]` with a `+x` layer (strength 0.2, order 1), `R0 = 1000 L`, `m = 0`, against the plane-strain PML kernel on the same strip at the origin: the complex frequencies of the first four in-plane modes agree to 2.1e-4, 6.7e-5, 2.3e-5, 8.1e-5 relative (`L / R0 = 1e-3`; the torsional modes are left out by their `u_theta` share).
* **Layer insensitivity** (T5): the wheel mode near 0.086, `Q = 121.84` with layers of thickness 3 and strength 3 (647 cells), 122.18 with thickness 6 (1161 cells) and 122.19 with strength 6: changes of 2.9e-3 in `Q` and 2.9e-5 in `Re f`, against the 5 % the plan asks for. The wheel holds 95 to 96 % of the mass of the mode.
* **K1 and K2 together, a disk on a post on a substrate, all touching the axis** (T5b, T6b, merged tree; the disk is `r` 0 to 8, 0.4 thick, the post `r` 0 to 1, the substrate `r` 0 to 20 and 3 deep, layers to the right and below, `E = rho = 1`, `nu = 0.3`, `m = 0`; the contour mode is within 10 % of the free disk's closed form): `Q = 2125.4` with layers of thickness 3 and strength 3 (830 cells), 2028.0 with thickness 6 (1310 cells), 2081.9 with strength 6; `Re f` changes by 3.2e-5 at most, `Q` by 4.6 % for the doubled thickness and 2.0 % for the doubled strength (the first is under the 5 % of the plan, with little margin on this coarse mesh). The untransformed form (`s_theta = 1`) gives `Q = 2126.1`, 2043.7, 2103.6: relative differences of 3.1e-4, 7.8e-3 and 1.0e-2, of the order of the insensitivity to the layer itself. So the two forms differ by about 1 % in `Q` here as they do on the annular wheel (T6 above), and the form of Bindel and Govindjee is not needed to reproduce their anchor loss to that accuracy.
* **The study on a solid disk that touches the axis** (`axisym_study.rs`): a thin free disk (`R = 1 mm`, `t = 20 um`) through the envelope, the typed problem and the library entry gives the same frequencies, and the contour mode is `1.774722e6 Hz` against the closed form `1.774765e6 Hz` (2.4e-5 relative); the log names the axis condition.
* **The whole path with the axis and the layers** (engine example 17 and the MCP test): a polysilicon-like disk on a post on a substrate, built by commands, gives the contour mode at 4.505e8 Hz (free disk 4.619e8) with `Q = 1733` and a layer fraction of 0.001, while the modes of the layers have layer fractions of 0.5 to 0.6 and `Q` of 2; on a mesh refined by 0.7 the `Q` of that mode changes by 9 % (the example is deliberately coarse).


## What was not verified

* The exact tie for `m = +-1`: converge-rate of an `m = +-1` mode that touches the axis was not measured beyond the rigid modes.
* Anisotropic materials on the axis: the kernel averages the stiffness about the axis (`average_about_axis`), as before.

* **A layer next to the axis.** T4 to T6 are off-axis and T5b and T6b have their layers far from it; whether `s_theta` inside a layer behaves near `r -> 0` does not arise, because a layer with a radial stretch lies away from the axis and a layer towards the axis (`x = minus`) is refused by the study (ADR 68).
* A complex stretch at `m != 0` is checked only through the unit and real stretch above and by T5/T6 at `m = 0`; there is no closed form for a complex stretch at `m != 0`.
* The `x = minus` direction of the kernel (the left layers of T5) is exercised only through the insensitivity of `Q`, with no separate check.
* The size of the reflection at the interface, which is the quantity the choice between the two forms is about, is not measured directly: T6 compares quality factors of one mode, not the reflection coefficient of a plane wave.
* The 3D-equivalent and the low-reflecting boundary (finding D1 of the plan: `lrb::damping_matrix` has no `r` weight) are untouched.

## Code

`crates/nyx-sms/src/{axisym,cross_section}.rs`, `crates/nyx-sms/tests/axisym_axis.rs`. Part 2: `crates/nyx-sms/src/axisym.rs` (`cylindrical_stretches`, the stiffness and mass), `crates/nyx-sms/src/cross_section.rs` (one line), `crates/femcore/src/pml.rs` (`radial_coordinate`, moved from `crates/nyx-ems/src/axisym.rs`), `crates/nyx-sms/tests/axisym_pml.rs`.

## Contract

None of its own: `CrossAssembly` gains the public fields `axis_dofs` and `pml_cells` (the latter from ADR 68); `kernel_stages` 1.4 (ADR 68) covers the stage API.
decisions.title: Axis conditions and the cylindrical stretch of the axisymmetric solid kernel

# 7. Metric-based mesh adaptation and structured PML layers, ported as `femcore::meshers`

Date: 2026-11-02

## Status

Accepted. The port (`7a9a85e`) was written by a separate session without access to nyx (see `docs/ports/meshers/HANDOFF.md`); 2D integration `3fbb24d`, 3D `44db967` to `fdb9f55`.

## Context

Hand-tuned meshes limited the accuracy of the chips and ring studies. Metric-based adaptation (Riemannian metrics from recovered Hessians or from physics) with local operators (split, collapse, flip, smooth) gives meshes sized to the field. Absorbing layers were unstructured triangles of uneven quality.

## Decision

* The mesher port lives in `femcore::meshers` as its own dimension-generic stack (`D = 2` or `3`): metrics (`adapt/metric.rs`), geometry oracles (`geom`, `geom3`), working meshes (`topo`, `topo3`), operators (`ops`, `ops3`), drivers (`drive`, `drive3`), PML generator (`adapt/pml.rs`), quality statistics, fixtures and a small independent Helmholtz validation harness (`validate/`).
* Constrained features (boundaries, material interfaces, corners, frozen faces) are classified from the labels and preserved exactly; periodic pairs stay congruent through frozen faces.
* Structured PML layers are generated around a box-shaped physical mesh: quads (2D) and prisms/hexes (3D), conforming, with `meshers::interop::pml_domains` producing the `Pml` description per layer label, and materials copied from the interface (`pml3`, `meshing_pml`).
* The **solve-estimate-adapt loop** (`estimate`, `estimate3`) recovers Hessians from a solution and feeds `adapt_to_metrics`; at order 1 it does not beat uniform meshes (Maxwell residual estimator needed), at order 2 it does.
* Everything is deterministic and bit-identical across thread counts (ADR 11).

## Consequences

* Adaptation is 2D and serial in the original port; 3D adds edge removal, flat-boundary flips and surface/crease collapses, still serial, with linear-time closest-point queries (`MISSING_FEATURES.md` section 3).
* PML reflection has been measured only for the 2D scalar problem; for the vector solvers only mesh convergence of damped modes and lossless equivalences are tested.
* Attempts at 30 split passes in a row degrade slivers; flips are interleaved. These lessons are in `ports/meshers/HANDOFF.md` section 9 and apply to any future threaded version.
* Provenance and licence (BSD-2-Clause) are recorded in `docs/ports/meshers/PROVENANCE.md` and `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`; whether BSD-2 is compatible with nyx's own licence has not been checked.

## Code

`crates/femcore/src/meshers/**`, `meshing.rs`, `meshing_pml.rs`, `pml3.rs`, `estimate.rs`, `estimate3.rs`, `refine3d.rs`. History: `7a9a85e`, `3fbb24d`, `154b64e`, `b9a135e`, `44db967`, `c49c4aa`, `281b2f8`, `79936d6`, `62d6cdc`, `ba625ec`, `fdb9f55`.

## Contract

`contracts/mesh`. The mesher's own acceptance tests are `tests/meshers.rs`, `adapt3d.rs`, `meshing.rs`, `physics_meshing.rs`.
decisions.title: Metric-based mesh adaptation and structured PML layers, ported as `femcore::meshers`

# 8. The ported solver library is merged but not wired into the physics

Date: 2026-10-31

## Status

Accepted as an interim state (commit `7a9a85e`, "Merge the solver and mesher ports into femcore"). The swap-in is open work. **Superseded by ADR 33** (phase 3 wired it and deleted the old modules).

## Context

`femsolve` (written in a separate repository, edition 2024, no access to nyx) provides one implementation of Krylov solvers, eigensolvers (Krylov-Schur, LOBPCG, Jacobi-Davidson, contour, Chebyshev filtering, NLEIGS, TOAR), preconditioners (ILU/ILUT/IC, Schwarz, AMG, AMS/ADS, field-split), sparse direct solvers with symbolic reuse and a thread policy, time steppers, optimisation, reduced-order sweeps and matrix-free operators, for real and complex scalars. nyx's physics runs on older modules (`eigen`, `lobpcg`, `amg`, `linalg`, `csparse`, `sparse`) that duplicate parts of it.

## Decision

* The library is moved in as `femcore::solvers` with its tests (`tests/solvers/*`), studies and CLI tools as examples (`fs_eps`, `fs_gen`, `fs_ksp`, `fs_contour`, `fs_snes`). The PETSc/SLEPc comparison harness stays in the original repository because nyx ships no Python.
* **No kernel calls it yet.** The integration order is in `docs/ports/solvers/NYX_INTEGRATION.md` (adapters, reproduce, compare, thread policy, swap the eigensolver behind `ShiftInvertEigenSolver`, keep the old one selectable). Its statements about nyx are unverified because its author could not see nyx.
* The stage boundary of ADR 9 is where a swap happens: "the backend is chosen in the solve stage, so a `femcore::solvers` adapter replaces one function per kernel".
* The library keeps determinism (fixed chunks, results bit-identical for every thread count; `NYX_THREADS` selects the pool through `crate::par`) and the `portable-kernels` feature, which trades the GEMM-based restart multiply for CPU-independent last bits.
* Licence: BSD-2-Clause with PETSc/SLEPc notices; compatibility with nyx's licence is unchecked.

## Consequences

* Duplicate AMG, LOBPCG, Arnoldi and four sparse-matrix types live side by side (R02).
* Any claim about the ported solvers' speed or robustness is about the library on its own test problems and the Linux VM it was written on, not about nyx runs.
* faer 0.24 is used by both stacks; the ported library touches it in two files only (`faer_glue.rs`, `direct.rs`).

## Code

`crates/femcore/src/solvers/**`, `examples/fs_*.rs`, `tests/solvers/**`, `docs/ports/solvers/*`; old stack `amg.rs`, `eigen.rs`, `lobpcg.rs`, `linalg.rs`, `csparse.rs`, `sparse.rs`.

## Contract

`contracts/kernel_stages`: each kernel's `solve_*` stage is the swap point and stays composition-equivalent to the one-call solver (`tests/stages.rs`).
decisions.title: The ported solver library is merged but not wired into the physics

decisions.content:
# 80. Modes carry what identifies them, and a convergence check follows a mode

Date: 2026-11-15

## Status

Proposed (capability R11, bookmark `capability-r11-sms-mode-scalars`, on `capability-r6-sms-axisym`). Amends ADR 68 (the result of the axisymmetric study gains scalars) and ADR 61 (`convergence_check` gains a way to pair solutions). Numbers 70 to 79 are reserved by other capability plans.

## Context

Benchmark A1 (Bindel and Govindjee 2005) was run through the MCP server as a product, and four things in the way were not physics:

1. A lossy mode's frequency was only the text `fN (Hz)` (`"6.93e8 +2.56e7i"`), which a host had to parse, while `QN` was a number.
2. Nothing said which family a mode belongs to. At `m = 0` the torsional modes (azimuthal displacement only) are solved together with the radial and axial ones, a flexural mode sits near the contour mode, and `layer fraction N` only separates the modes of the layers. The benchmark summed squares of node values, which is not the energy and needs every field read back.
3. `convergence_check` compares solution `i` with solution `i`. The order of the complex modes of an open resonator changes between meshes (a layer mode moves past a resonator mode), so the check reported a relative difference near 1 for a mode that had moved by 1e-4.
4. The study did not say that `m = 0` holds torsional modes, or that the number of modes returned can differ from `n_modes`.

## Decision

**Scalars per mode of `axisymmetric_eigenfrequency`** (stage `cross_section_fields`), additive:

* `f re N (Hz)` and `f im N (Hz)`: the two parts of the eigenvalue as numbers, for every mode, with or without loss. The scalar `fN (Hz)` keeps its form (a number without loss, text with loss; `physics_sms_result` 1.1), because removing it breaks hosts for no gain.
* `radial share N`, `axial share N`, `azimuthal share N`: the split of `int rho |u|^2 r dr dz` over the three displacement components, taken over the cells outside the absorbing layers. They sum to 1.
* `share in domain <label> N` for each domain outside the layers that has mass: the same integral per domain. They sum to 1. The kernel knows domain numbers only; the engine replaces `domain <label>` by the region name after the solve (`solve::name_domains`), so a host sees `share in disk N`. A caller of the kernel without an engine sees the numbers.

The integrals are computed by `axisym::mode_energy_axisym` in one pass over the cells (the integrand and quadrature of `assemble_mass_axisym`, no stretch), not by one mass matrix per domain. They are mass-weighted, so they are shares of the kinetic energy of the physical displacement. `layer fraction N` is unchanged.

**`convergence_check` pairs solutions** (`convergence::Matching`), additive:

* `match`: `"index"` (default: nothing changes for existing callers) or `"nearest"`. With `nearest` each solution of the present mesh is paired with the nearest eigenvalue of the finer mesh in the complex plane (distance over the larger modulus), and a pair is kept only when the two are each other's nearest (mutual nearest neighbours). No threshold is asked of the caller.
* `track: { f }`: only the solution whose eigenvalue has its real part nearest `f` is compared, against the nearest eigenvalue of the finer mesh. It implies `nearest`; with `match: "index"` it is refused.
* With pairing, the rows are the eigenvalue, the value and the per-mode scalars of each pair, named with the index of the mode on the present mesh; `pairs` lists `{ coarse, refined, distance }`, `unpaired` the solutions of each mesh without a partner; `worst_relative` and `converged` cover the paired modes only, and the note says so. Scalars that do not belong to a mode are not compared in this form.
* A per-mode scalar is recognised by its name: the one-based mode number at the end, before a unit in brackets if there is one (`Q3`, `layer fraction 3`, `f re 3 (Hz)`). This is a naming convention of results, not a field of `SolveResult`.

**Descriptions.** The study doc states the new scalars, that `m = 0` includes torsional modes, and that the modes returned are the converged eigenpairs nearest `f_search` (the block Krylov-Schur run returns the pairs whose residual is below 1e-6: fewer than `n_modes` when some did not converge, more when a block converged past it). This is how the solver behaves, not a defect, so it is described and not changed. The guide card says that Q converges slower than f, to refine at re-entrant corners, and to compare meshes with `match` or `track`.

**`benchmark_a1.rs` is removed** from `crates/nyx-engine/tests`. Benchmarks are not nyx software (paul, 2026-11-14): no benchmark driver and no test asserting a paper's number lives in the repository. The closed-form tests and example 17 remain the regression guards of the study.

## Consequences

* A host picks a mode by numbers: small `layer fraction`, `radial share` and `share in disk` large, nearest a frequency. No field needs to be read.
* Pairing by eigenvalue alone can pair two different modes that cross between meshes; the mutual rule drops most of these and `distance` shows how far a pair moved. Pairing by field overlap would be stricter and needs both fields on one mesh; not done.
* The convention for per-mode scalar names is implicit. A scalar of another physics that ends in a number within the range of the solutions is taken as a per-mode scalar when pairing is asked for. Recorded in `ROUGH_SPOTS.md` (R11a).
* `convergence_check` still refines only the global element size and its rules, not the sizes of `add_size` features (ADR 61 as it was). On the model that asked for the pairing, the A1 disk, the resolution is set by such sizes, so the check follows the right mode but tests the bulk mesh only. The tool description and the guide card say so; scaling size features is recorded as R11b and not done here.
* The same scalars are the natural next step for `ems` (`axisymmetric_modes`, `cavity`), and for the 2D and 3D complex eigenfrequency kernels of `sms` (`pml.rs`, `lrb.rs`), which still give only the text frequency. Not done here.
* Contracts: `physics_sms_result` 1.2, `physics_sms` 1.4, `engine_commands` and `mcp_tools` next minor, `kernel_stages` 1.5 (all additive).

## What was verified

`crates/nyx-sms/tests/axisym_mode_scalars.rs`: `f re` and `f im` equal the eigenvalue for lossless and lossy modes; the shares sum to 1; the torsional mode of a solid cylinder has azimuthal share 1 and the radial plane-strain mode radial share 1 (thresholds in the test); a two-domain body's domain shares sum to 1; a layer has no share. `crates/nyx-engine/tests/examples.rs`: on example 17 the shares appear under the region names and the contour mode is radial and in the disk; `convergence_check` with `nearest` pairs or lists every mode, `track` gives one mode, `index` is unchanged, bad arguments are refused. `crates/nyx-mcp/tests/stdio.rs`: the scalars and the two new arguments over stdio. The A1 reference case rerun on a build of this bookmark gives the numbers of the build before it (recorded with the benchmark, outside the repository).

## What was not verified

Pairing on a case where two resonator modes cross between meshes; the shares for `|m| >= 1` against a closed form (the sums are checked, the split is not); the window (it shows the scalars of a result generically).

## Code

`crates/nyx-sms/src/{axisym,cross_section,lib}.rs`, `crates/nyx-sms/tests/axisym_mode_scalars.rs`, `crates/nyx-engine/src/{convergence,commands,solve}.rs`, `crates/nyx-engine/cards/nyx-instructions.md`, `crates/nyx-engine/tests/examples.rs`, `crates/nyx-mcp/tests/stdio.rs`, `docs/architecture/contracts/`.

## Contract

`physics_sms_result` 1.2, `physics_sms` 1.4, `engine_commands` 1.7 (1.6 is the A3 line), `mcp_tools` 2.3, `kernel_stages` 1.5.
decisions.title: Modes carry what identifies them, and a convergence check follows a mode

# 82. Curved (isoparametric, quadratic) tetrahedra for the `ems` cavity study; amends ADR 18

Date: 2026-11-15

## Status

Implemented on `capability-r12-curved-elements` (default off; paul decides later whether it becomes the default). Amends ADR 18, which deferred curved nodes.

## Context

The 3D lattice mesher (ADR 40) fits boundary vertices to the exact surface but the cells are straight, so a sphere is a polyhedron and the geometric error is O(h^2) whatever the element order (ADR 18). The A7 simple-cubic cross-check against MPB (`benchmarks/johnson-joannopoulos-2001`, part 2) failed its pre-declared limits by exactly that error: it falls as h^2 and its sign flips between a dielectric and an air sphere.

## Decision

* **Storage.** `CellMesh<D>::edge_nodes: Vec<([u32; 2], [f64; D])>`: for an edge (sorted vertex pair) the position of its mid-edge geometry node, sorted by pair, empty by default. An edge not listed is straight (its node is the midpoint). The solver mesh (`mesh::SimplexMesh`) carries the same list by edge index (`edge_node`, `cell_is_curved`, `cell_geometry_nodes`, `edge_node_list`). Round trips (`Mesh::from_solver_mesh`, `discretise`, `from_cells`) keep it; `from_cells` drops it when cells had to be split; refinement and adaptation start from lists that are empty. HDF5 mesh files carry two optional datasets (`/mesh/edge_node_pairs`, `/mesh/edge_node_points`); a file without them is a straight mesh. XDMF output keeps straight cells.
* **Placing the nodes** (`femcore::meshing::curve3`). For every edge of a boundary or interface facet `Domain3::project_edge` gives the surface position of the midpoint; it is kept when it moved by more than `1e-9` and less than `0.25` of the edge length (a planar face adds nothing). Every curved cell must keep `det J > 0.1 det J_straight` at its ten nodes and at the points of a degree-6 rule; if not, the offsets of its curved edges are halved (every cell around an edge sees the same offset), and after four halvings the edges are straightened. `CurveReport` counts curved edges and cells, relaxed and straightened edges and the smallest scaled Jacobian. An edge whose ends lie on two faces that place its midpoint differently (a crease) stays straight (`Domain3::edge_on_crease`). Independent of the thread count.
* **Switch.** `MeshSettings.curved`, `MeshRequest.curved`, `GeomMeshOpts.curved`, `set_mesh` argument `curved`; default false and not serialised when false, so every existing project, golden and example is byte-identical. After an adaptation or structured layers the edges are curved last (`curve_solver_mesh`).
* **Kernel.** `femcore::fem::CurvedTet` (ten nodes, quadratic Lagrange map, `jacobian(lam) -> (J^-T grad_ref lambda_a, det J)`), `quad_rule_collapsed(degree)` (Gauss on a collapsed cube, any degree). `nyx-ems::cavity::assemble_maxwell` integrates cells with a curved edge with a degree-6 rule and, at each point, the gradients `g_a(q)` of the barycentric functions in place of the constant ones: `basis3` is unchanged, because `lam_a g_b - lam_b g_a` is then exactly the covariant Piola image of the Whitney function and `2 g_a x g_b` equals `J curl_ref / det J`; the order-2 gradient and face functions follow by the product rule. Cells with no curved edge keep the affine path and the same arithmetic (the matrices of a straight mesh are unchanged). The discrete gradient, numbering, periodic relations and reduction are topological and unchanged. `emw_eigen_fields` evaluates `E` with the same per-point gradients.
* **Other physics.** `sms` and `dfs` ignore `edge_nodes` (they see straight cells); only the `ems` cavity study uses them.

## Consequences

* Closed forms (tests on the bookmark): the volume of a meshed unit sphere is 2.1e-5 off at h = r/4 (straight 1.3e-2) and falls at about h^4.5 against h^2 for straight; the lowest triplet of a PEC sphere cavity converges at rate 2.96 (curved) against 2.10 (straight) over h = r/5 to r/7, and at h = r/3.5 the error is 3.5e-5 against 6.4e-3. A constant field is represented exactly on a quadratic image of a box, and the curl of the basis equals the curl of its field by finite differences.
* Rough spots (`ROUGH_SPOTS.md` R32 to R35): plotted quadratic nodes stay at the straight positions; sms and dfs see straight cells; creases and a curved face meeting a periodic face stay straight (`capability-r7-periodic-cells` must give matching curved edges on a paired face); curved cells inside a PML are allowed but untested; the volume integrals of `nyx-analysis` (mode volume, layer fraction) use straight measures.
* Contracts: `mesh_cells` 1.1, `mesh_request` 1.1, `mesh_report` 1.1, `engine_commands` 1.8 (1.6 is A3, 1.7 is R11), `mcp_tools` 2.4 (2.3 is R11); `results_file` additive (optional datasets).

## Code

`crates/femcore/src/fem.rs` (`CurvedTet`, `quad_rule_collapsed`), `mesh/cells.rs`, `mesh/mod.rs`, `mesh/exchange.rs`, `meshing/curve3.rs`, `meshing/geomdrive3.rs`, `crates/nyx-ems/src/cavity.rs`, `crates/nyx-engine/src/h5io.rs`.
decisions.title: Curved (isoparametric, quadratic) tetrahedra for the `ems` cavity study; amends ADR 18

# 83. Size rules on faces and `max_dev` act in the 3D lattice mesher

Date: 2026-11-15

## Status

Implemented on `capability-r12-curved-elements`.

## Context

`GeomDomain3` kept only the `Size` rules on regions, and `max_dev` was read only by the adaptive path, so `add_size` on a face and `max_dev` were accepted and silently ignored in 3D. Separately, the `set_mesh` command rejected `max_dev`, `structured_pml` and `points_per_wavelength` as unknown fields although its schema lists them and the window sends them (found while doing this work, fixed here).

## Decision

* Per face, `h_face = min(rule h, 2 sqrt(2 r max_dev))`, the second term for a face with a radius of curvature `r` (`facet_radius`, the formula of `adapt3d`); `max_dev` comes from a rule on the face or from the request (`GeomDomain3::with_max_dev`). With no `max_dev` the lattice path has no chord limit, so existing meshes do not change (the adaptive path keeps its `h / 50` default).
* `Domain3::size_at(p)` returns the smallest `h_face + 0.3 d` over faces at distance `d` from `p` (growth 0.3 per length: a ratio of 1.3 between neighbours); step 8 of `mesh_3d` uses `min(region size, size_at)` and runs when any face asks for less than the global size (`asks_size_at`). New boundary vertices are placed on the exact face by `project_edge`.
* A `Size` rule on crease edges or vertices has no meaning in 3D, `min_layers` has no effect, and a `max_deviation` on a region cannot apply: `MeshReport.warnings` names each instead of silence.
* A face size that reaches a periodic face is refused with a message (the pair would be refined differently); congruent periodic faces are R30 of `capability-r7-periodic-cells`.
* `set_mesh` accepts `max_dev`, `structured_pml`, `points_per_wavelength` and `curved`.

## Consequences

Meshes without a face size or `max_dev` are unchanged (tested). `mesh_report` 1.1 gains `warnings` and `curved`.

## Code

`crates/femcore/src/meshing/geomdrive3.rs`, `mesher3d.rs`, `request.rs`; `crates/nyx-engine/src/commands.rs`.
decisions.title: Size rules on faces and `max_dev` act in the 3D lattice mesher

# 84. Results are stale per physics: the key is the problem key

Date: 2026-11-16

## Status

Accepted by paul (productivity plan question 1, 2026-11-16). **Number 84: settled at the merge of the productivity line with main (2026-11-19), the next free number after the capability line.** Refines ADR 64 (cache keys); implements step P1 of `docs/NYX2_PRODUCTIVITY_PLAN.md`.

## Context

A result was stamped with a hash of the whole project, so any edit made every result stale, and the window dropped the flag that the engine already returned: a plot of a solve from before an edit looked current. Two solves of one physics could finish out of order (an AI host can start two) and the last to finish became the stored result whatever it was made from.

## Decision

* **The key of a result is the problem key of its physics** (`Engine::problem_key`): a hash of that physics' problem, the materials the project carries, the mesh key (geometry, mesh settings, sizing) and the problem keys of the physics it takes fields from (its imports, found through the `exports` and `imports` of the `Physics` trait, as `solve_order` does). The active physics, the title and everything about how a result is looked at (colormap, camera, field, range) are not in it. A result is *stale* when its key is not the key its physics has now. Staleness follows the content: undoing an edit makes the result current again.
* **It is a cache key in the sense of ADR 64**: computed in the process, never stored in a file, never sent. The replies of the commands carry `stale` and `age_s`, not the key.
* **Late jobs.** A finished solve replaces the stored result of a physics only when its key is the one the physics has now, or when the stored result is stale and the job started later (jobs are numbered in the order they start). Otherwise it is recorded in the run table but not stored; the reply says `current` and `stored` per result. The same rule keeps an old mesh from displacing the mesh of the project. A run is recorded with the mesh of its own job.
* **The window** shows a stale result as stale: a mark on the plot, a band with "Solve again" in the Results tab and panel, "(stale)" in the list of results. A result is stale for the window when the engine says so, when a newer result of the physics replaced it, or when the Geometry or Mesh tab holds edits that were not applied to the engine yet.

## Known limits

* **Not an identity ("same key, same numbers").** `run_chain` hands a physics the fields of the physics that were *in the same job*, so `solve_run` of `sms` alone and of `dfs, sms` have the same `sms` key and different numbers. For staleness this is acceptable: both are results of the current problem. A later use of the key to deduplicate work (the queue, plan step Q1) must add what was chained.
* **The whole `materials` map of the project is hashed**, not only the entries a problem names, so editing a project material that a physics does not use stales it. This errs on the safe side; the library files are loaded once per session and are not in the key.
* **A mesh sized from the physics** (`physics_sizing`) puts the wavelengths of every physics in the mesh key, so a wavelength edit then stales every result on that mesh. That is correct (the mesh is different); with `physics_sizing` off it stales only its own physics.
* The key is computed on each call (no cache): about 0.2 ms for the examples and 5 ms at a project of 1,000 features (measured, `docs/PRODUCTIVITY_STATUS.md`). Caching waits for a model that needs it.

## Consequences

* An edit of one physics no longer marks the others stale; an edit of the geometry still marks all.
* An MCP host sees `stale` on every answer that quotes a result; it cannot quote a stale number without the JSON saying so.

## Code

`crates/nyx-engine/src/engine.rs` (`problem_key`, `problem_keys`, `is_stale`, `apply`), `commands.rs`, `analyse.rs`, `results_file.rs`, `crates/app/src/{app,tabs}.rs`; tests `crates/nyx-engine/tests/stale.rs` and the window tests `a_result_on_show_says_when_the_model_changed`, `a_result_the_engine_did_not_keep_is_not_put_on_show`.

## Contract

`engine_commands` 1.9: descriptions of `result_info`, `result_field`, `analyse`, `list_analyses`; replies gain `stale`, `age_s`, `current`, `stored`.
decisions.title: Results are stale per physics: the key is the problem key

# 85. Every long operation is a job that can be watched and cancelled

Date: 2026-11-16

## Status

Accepted as a step of the productivity plan (P2, `docs/NYX2_PRODUCTIVITY_PLAN.md`). **Number 85: settled at the merge of the productivity line with main (2026-11-19), the next free number after the capability line.** **Depends on ADR 84 (P1)**: this bookmark is built on `productivity-1-stale` and cannot merge without it. Builds on ADR 57 (the front-ends are thin) and ADR 61 (convergence is an engine command).

## Context

Measured in P0 (`docs/PRODUCTIVITY_STATUS.md`): the window froze for 0.35 to 1.3 s after every recorded run while it wrote `results.h5`, and for 0.1 to 0.3 s in `open_results` (read, a blocking re-mesh, compare); a mesh job could not be cancelled and logged no stage; a mesh convergence check ran on a bare thread with no cancel, no progress and no place in the job list, beside whatever else the window started.

## Decision

* **A mesh is a cancellable job with stages.** `start_mesh` installs the job's `Progress` and `FemcoreMesher::mesh` opens a stage; the adaptive drivers (2D and 3D, each iteration and each split cascade) and the 3D lattice mesher (between its phases) check the cancel flag. Checks are on the driving thread, not inside parallel passes (worker threads do not see the progress), so a cancel lands at the next pass boundary. A cancelled mesh is `Cancelled`, not an invalid model.
* **A convergence check is a job** (`Engine::start_convergence`, `convergence_check {wait: false}`). Its two solves run on the job's thread under its `Progress`, as two stages, through the same `run_chain` as a solve; it is listed by `job_list`, reports its stage and is cancelled by `job_cancel`. The synchronous command (default `wait: true`) is unchanged for hosts.
* **Opening a results file is a job** (`start_open_results`, `open_results {wait: false}`): reading, meshing again and the comparison with the stored mesh run on the job; the engine is not touched until the job is applied, then the file's project replaces the project and the stored results become the latest results (stored under the keys of ADR 84). A failed or cancelled open changes nothing, with no restore step. The window makes its draft workflow when the job ends. (The plan proposed showing the stored results against the stored mesh at once and re-meshing as the job; the whole open as a job removes the freeze without the viewer having to draw from a mesh no model exists for.)
* **Writing a results file is a job** (`start_export_results`, `export_results {wait: false}`) that writes a snapshot of the project, mesh and results of the moment of the request, to a temporary name that is renamed when the file is complete. The window starts it after each recorded run and goes on; a failure shows when the job ends.
* **Honest cancel.** `JobInfo` carries `cancel_requested` and `stage_seconds` (job_status and job_list), and the toolbar shows the seconds in the stage the job waits for; a cancel lasts as long as the stage it is in cannot be interrupted (a factorisation), and nothing estimates it.
* **A job started for a project that was replaced is dropped.** The engine counts the projects it has held (`set_project`); a mesh or solve that ends for an earlier one returns an error and changes nothing (it would otherwise store its result into the new project, ADR 84's rule for an empty slot).
* **Gate:** a test reads the window's sources and fails when they call `mesh_now`, `solve_now`, `engine.wait`, `open_results`, `export_results` or `convergence_check` (the headless `batch.rs` may wait).

## Not in this decision

* **A queue.** The window keeps its one running job and its one waiting slot; running several jobs in order, shared between the window and a host, is the scheduler of plan step Q1 (ADR [87]).
* **Cancel inside a factorisation or an assembly pass**: not possible in process; the way to stop one at once is a child process (plan step P4).
* **Waiting for a pending results file when the window closes**: the temporary name means a closed window leaves no file that looks complete, but the file of the last run can be missing.

## Consequences

* The window can no longer be frozen by the engine on its own thread; the first 3D freeze measured in P0 is gone.
* `job_status` and `job_list` gain two fields; `convergence_check`, `export_results` and `open_results` gain `wait`; `solve_run`-style replies are unchanged.
* Edits made in the window while a results file is being opened are lost when the file's project replaces it (the old window could not be edited during the open).

## Code

`crates/nyx-engine/src/{engine,jobs,convergence,results_file,meshing,commands}.rs`, `crates/femcore/src/adapt/{drive,drive3}.rs`, `crates/femcore/src/meshing/mesher3d.rs`, `crates/app/src/{app,shell,tabs}.rs`; tests `crates/nyx-engine/tests/jobs.rs` and the window tests in `app.rs`.

## Contract

`engine_commands` 1.10: `convergence_check`, `export_results`, `open_results` take `wait`; replies of `job_status` and `job_list` gain `cancel_requested` and `stage_seconds`. `mcp_tools` 2.5: the same three tools take `wait`.
decisions.title: Every long operation is a job that can be watched and cancelled

# 86. Solves run in a worker process; their memory is estimated from what workers measured

Date: 2026-11-17

## Status

Accepted as step P4 of the productivity plan (`docs/NYX2_PRODUCTIVITY_PLAN.md`, section 3), with Paul's answers of 2026-11-17: child processes are essential, and every solve of the window and of the MCP server runs in one by default. **Number 86: settled at the merge of the productivity line with main (2026-11-19), the next free number after the capability line.** Builds on the job runner and the queue (ADR 85, 87) and on the results file (ADR 62, 63); step Q2 (estimates and admission) is part of it.

## Context

A 3D solve can need more memory than the machine has (the A7 meshes need about 22 GB; a 109k-unknown cavity measured 10.7 GB in P0) and a factorisation cannot be interrupted, so a cancel can last minutes. In one process, running out of memory takes the window or the MCP server with every other thing it holds, and "cancel requested" cannot be honoured at once. P0 measured what a child process costs: about 0.07 s on a 2D solve that takes 0.01 s, 0.16 s on a 12k-unknown 3D cavity, 0.27 s (7 %) at 39k unknowns (`examples/isolate_cost.rs`).

## Decision

* **A solve job can run in a child process, the worker.** `nyx_engine::worker` holds both sides. The parent (`run_remote`) writes the frozen project (JSON), the materials of the library the job sees (TOML by name) and the chain of physics into a temporary folder and starts `PROGRAM --job FOLDER`. The worker (`serve`) builds a scratch `Engine` from them and runs the same `start_solve` path the in-process job runs, so the numbers cannot differ (ADR 11); `tests/worker.rs` compares every physics of five examples and a coupled chain, **to the bit** (scalars, eigenvalues, every field value), and the materials by their TOML and their debug text.
* **Results come back as the results file** (`results.h5`, the writer and reader of ADR 62 and 63), the same round trip as opening a file. The parent holds a mesh of its own (it draws on it) and checks that the stored mesh is that mesh (meshing is deterministic, ADR 55); a difference fails the job with a message naming a worker of another version. A build without the `hdf5` feature cannot isolate.
* **What the worker says** is on its standard output, one line per message starting with `@nyx ` and holding JSON; other output is ignored: `status` every 100 ms (the stage, how long it has been in it, the fraction, the stage log when it changed) and one `done` (the error if the chain failed, whether results were written, the peak working set and peak commit of the process). The parent copies each `status` into the job's `Progress` (`Progress::mirror`), so `job_status`, `queue_get` and the toolbar show a worker's stage exactly as they show an in-process one. The last line of the log says what the worker used (`worker process: peak memory ...`).
* **Cancel kills the process.** The parent polls the job's cancel flag every 40 ms and kills the child, even in the middle of a factorisation: measured under 1.5 s on the 3D cavity, where an in-process cancel waits for the stage. A killed or crashed worker (exit without a `done`: an abort, an out-of-memory failure, a kill from outside) fails its job with the exit code and what the worker wrote on stderr, and says nothing else was affected; the next queued job starts by itself (`tests/worker_crash.rs`, with a crash drill `NYX_WORKER_DRILL=abort`).
* **The worker ends with its parent.** It exits when its standard input closes, so no solve runs on for nobody. On Windows it starts without a console window and, like the programs that host an engine, opts out of power throttling (`process.rs`, P0b), which would otherwise move a piped background process to the efficiency cores.
* **Which program is the worker.** The front-ends are their own workers: `nyx` and `nyx-mcp` answer `--job FOLDER` before anything else (`Engine::set_self_as_worker(true)`, called by `main`, never by a test, where the program would be the test runner). Nothing else has to be built or shipped. A small `nyx-worker` program (a `[[bin]]` of `nyx-engine`) does the same for the engine's tests.
* **Default and per request.** With `set_worker(program, by_default)` every solve of that engine runs in a worker unless the request says `isolate: false`; `solve_run`, `queue_submit` and `sweep_run` take `isolate`. A request that **asks** for isolation (`isolate: true`) and cannot have it (no worker, an engine with a registry or mesher of its own, a build without HDF5) fails with the reason; a solve that is isolated only **by default** runs in the process as before.
* **Memory is measured where it can be.** A process's peak memory (`process::peak_memory`: peak working set and peak commit on Windows, the high-water marks of `/proc` on Linux) is the worker's own, so it belongs to one run; in the process of a window it would be the peak of everything the window did. The `solve_run` answer carries `worker: { peak_working_set, peak_commit }`.
* **Estimates are learned from the workers, never invented** (`estimate.rs`, step Q2). Each worker run that finished its chain adds a row (the chain's physics, the dimension, the cells, the unknowns, the peak working set and commit, the seconds) to the engine's history, kept as JSON lines in `solve_history.jsonl` in the workspace folder by the window and the MCP server and shared by appending. Before a solve starts, once its mesh is known, the rows of the same chain and dimension are fitted with a power law of memory against cells. **With fewer than two sizes there is no estimate** and the solve starts as before; a size outside those seen says `extrapolated`; the answer carries the number of runs, the exponent and the margin (the largest error the fit makes on its own rows, at least 10 %). P0 measured memory growing as the 1.5th power of the unknowns on the 3D cavity, so no constant per unknown is used. The estimate is in the `queue_get` / `queue_list` entry of the job (`estimate`: bytes, bytes_with_margin, seconds, runs, extrapolated, exponent).
* **Admission.** A solve whose estimate with margin is above 90 % of the machine's physical memory is refused at once (`force: true` starts it anyway), because it could not run with nothing else on the machine. One that fits the machine but not what is free now (another program, the window and the MCP server both solving) **waits**, showing the stage "waiting for memory: needs about 9.0 GB, 6.0 GB free", asking again every 250 ms until it fits, and a cancel ends the wait. Free memory is asked of the system (`process::system_memory`, replaceable in tests), so two programs each check it before they start.
* **Backfill is not built.** The heavy lane runs one job at a time (all solvers use every core: two solves at once gain nothing), so a waiting job holds the lane and there is nothing to backfill into; the item that is waiting for memory is the job in the lane. It is worth building if the heavy lane ever runs several jobs. The time estimate is shown, never used to decide.

## Not in this decision

* **Convergence checks run in the process** (two solves inside one job); they get a worker with the same estimate and admission as a solve when step Q2 lands.
* **A workspace-wide queue shared by the window and the MCP server** (plan Q3): two programs still each run a heavy job. Workers make this survivable (a crash fails one job), not coordinated.
* **Workers on other machines** (plan Q4).
* **Streaming results** instead of a file. The file is written and read once per run; if it ever matters at 3D sizes, the cost shows in `isolate_cost`.

## Consequences

* A solve of 0.01 s costs about 0.07 s in a worker. Paul chose isolation everywhere over a size threshold.
* `engine_commands` gains the argument `isolate` (a description-level and additive change, provisional version) and the `solve_run` answer a `worker` object.
* The window needs nothing beyond `main`'s call; the toolbar's "cancel requested" now ends at once for a solve.

## Code

`crates/nyx-engine/src/{worker,estimate,engine,jobs,queue,process}.rs`, `crates/nyx-engine/src/bin/nyx-worker.rs`, `crates/femcore/src/progress.rs` (`mirror`), `crates/app/src/{main,app}.rs`, `crates/nyx-mcp/src/main.rs`, `crates/nyx-engine/examples/isolate_cost.rs`; tests `crates/nyx-engine/tests/{worker,worker_crash,admission}.rs`.
decisions.title: Solves run in a worker process; their memory is estimated from what workers measured

# 87. Work is queued in lanes; stages are shared by content

Date: 2026-11-16

## Status

Accepted as a step of the productivity plan (Q1, `docs/NYX2_PRODUCTIVITY_PLAN.md` section 3a). **Number 87: settled at the merge of the productivity line with main (2026-11-19), the next free number after the capability line.** **Depends on ADR 84 (P1) and ADR 85 (P2)**: this bookmark is built on `productivity-2-jobs` and cannot merge without both. Builds on ADR 57 (the front-ends are thin), ADR 64 (cache keys, never persisted) and ADR 84 (the problem key).

## Context

The runner started every job on a thread of its own at once. The engine refused nothing, so a host could start three solves and they ran together on the one rayon pool with their memory added up; the window kept its own "one at a time" rule beside it. A request that came after another of the same project meshed again, and a convergence check re-solved the mesh the user had just solved.

## Decision

* **Jobs run in lanes.** The *heavy* lane (mesh, solve, convergence check, opening a results file: they hold every core and the memory) runs one job at a time. The *light* lane (writing a results file) runs beside it, two at a time. The lane is fixed by the kind of job; nothing guesses a size (estimates are plan step Q2).
* **A job submitted while its lane is busy waits in the queue, and the runner starts the next one itself** when a job ends, from the finishing job's own thread. No front-end has to poll for the queue to move; `wait` works on a queued job. The state `queued` is new, `JobInfo` carries `lane`, `owner`, `priority`, `held`, `position` and `queued_seconds`.
* **Order:** priority (1 a person's request, 2 an agent's, 3 sweeps and batches; the window's engine is the owner `gui` and defaults to 1, others to 2), with ageing (a waiting job competes one level higher after a minute, never above 1); then the owner served longest ago (round robin, so a 50-point sweep of an agent delays a person by at most one item); then submission order. The order never enters a number: a job carries a frozen copy of the project (it always did) and reads no state another job left (a test submits the same three solves in three orders and compares the numbers bit for bit).
* **Cancel, hold, supersede, pause.** A queued job that is cancelled never runs and finishes `Cancelled` at once; a request cancelled before it ran leaves no run record. `hold` keeps a queued job from starting until `release`; `supersede` (a key of the kind and targets) cancels a queued job of the same owner and key when a newer one arrives, which is what a new Compute of the same target does; `pause` stops anything new from starting.
* **Stages are shared by content.** The engine keeps the last two meshes by mesh key and the last eight solve summaries by `(problem key, chain)`. A solve or mesh request that finds its mesh there does not build it ("mesh: the same mesh was built by an earlier request" in its log); a convergence check whose coarse solve (the physics alone on the present mesh) is there uses its numbers and solves only the finer mesh (`coarse_reused: true`, and a log line). The cache key includes the **chain** (the targets of the job that solved it), because the problem key alone is not enough: a physics solved alone and the same physics solved with the physics it imports from share a key and not their numbers (the limit recorded in ADR 84). A cancelled request keeps the mesh it built if it had built it. The summaries are the numbers a check compares, not the fields.
* **A failure stops the chain after it, not before it.** `run_chain_partial` returns the physics solved before the one that failed; the engine stores them (they are valid results of their own problems), records the run as failed and returns the error. A cancel discards the chain as before.
* **Sweeps are a queue of points, and a point is an edit list.** `sweep_run` takes `points` (each a list of `{ cmd, args }`: any command whose access is `edit` except those that replace the project) or `series` (one command repeated with a field set to each value), applies them to copies of the project and checks them all before anything is submitted (a bad point fails the request, naming it, and nothing runs), then submits one solve per point to the heavy lane at priority 3. What varies is the case's to say: a geometry parameter, the wavelength in the study, a material, a mesh setting, several at once. Each point is a job with its own frozen project, uses the stage caches (points that share a mesh build it once), is recorded in the run table as its own run (`StoreLink::record_point` freezes the point's project in the run and does *not* commit it as the experiment's project) and never touches the engine's project, mesh or results: the table (`sweep_table`, optionally waiting `wait_s`) holds each point's numbers, unknowns, cells and run, and a result's fields are dropped after the run is written. `sweep_cancel` cancels the points that have not finished; a point cancelled before it ran leaves no record. A point's numbers equal those of the same edits made by hand (a test compares them bit for bit) and do not depend on the order of the points. The azimuthal sweep of capability R9 becomes a thin command over this at merge.
* **Commands.** `queue_submit` (solve, mesh or convergence), `queue_list`, `queue_get`, `queue_cancel`, `queue_hold`, `queue_release`, `queue_set_priority`, `queue_pause`, `queue_resume`, and `queue_wait` with a **required** `timeout_s`, which returns the job's entry with `waiting: true` at the timeout instead of blocking for ever. `job_wait` takes the same optional `timeout_s`. An entry says what was asked (`kind`, `targets`) and whether the project has changed since (`project_changed`).

## Not in this decision

* **Estimates and admission by memory** (plan Q2, with P4): the heavy lane's limit is one job, not a memory budget.
* **A queue shared by the window and an MCP server** (Q3): each process has its own engine and queue; two processes still run their heavy jobs together.
* **Stage graphs with refcounted nodes.** Requests share a mesh and a coarse solve through the content cache; a request is still one job, not a graph of stages that fail and cancel separately. The partial result of a failed chain is the one case that crosses that line.
* **Fair share by an owner's permissions** (an AI host may only cancel its own requests) and moving an item up or down by drag; the priority number is the order control.

## Consequences

* `start_solve` and the other starters return at once with an id as before, but the job may be queued; `job_status` says so. Code that assumed two jobs run at the same time (a test that holds one job while waiting for the next) needs a gate; none in the tree did.
* Two solves that a host starts with `wait: false` now run one after the other, in order of priority.

## Code

`crates/nyx-engine/src/{jobs,queue,sweep,engine,solve,convergence,commands,store_link}.rs`; tests `crates/nyx-engine/tests/{queue,sweep}.rs`.

## Contract

`engine_commands` 1.11: the ten `queue_*` commands, `job_wait` takes `timeout_s`, the replies of `job_status` and `job_list` gain the queue fields, `convergence_check` gains `coarse_reused`. `mcp_tools` 2.6: the same tools. `engine_commands` 1.12 and `mcp_tools` 2.7: `sweep_run`, `sweep_table`, `sweep_cancel`.
decisions.title: Work is queued in lanes; stages are shared by content
